detail.abstract: Referees increasingly use large language models (LLMs), while finance and accounting journals disagree about whether to allow it. We ask which part of a referee's job the models can do. GPT-4o, whose training data end before the 2024 conference season, referees the papers presented at the 2024 AFA and NBER finance meetings, and we compare its verdicts with publication in the top-three finance journals over the next two years. Papers the model scores one standard deviation higher are 44% more likely to be published, net of author reputation. The result is not driven by look-ahead bias, as the model does not recall the outcomes. The information comes from its judgements of correctness and exposition. Its judgements of originality and significance carry none, and a referee guide that stresses importance does not help. The split between correctness and contribution holds for accounting papers and for a newer model, GPT-5. LLMs can check whether research is right, but not whether it matters. The technical check can go to the model, while the judgement of contribution stays with people.

title: The Primal-Dual Newsvendor: Data-Driven Network Inventory without Solvers
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Primal-Dual Newsvendor: Data-Driven Network Inventory without Solvers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no declaration of interest.

detail.abstract: Modern commerce and industry operate networks of resources in various combinations to serve customer demand for products and services. Examples include assemble-to-order (ATO) systems for computer and automobile production, network revenue management in the airline and hotel industries, and service networks in healthcare. Inventory and capacity decisions in these networks are difficult for two reasons: i) serving customers requires coordinated resource availability across the network, and ii) economies of scale mean up-front decisions entail fixed costs and batch sizes (e.g., inventory batched in pallets or truckloads, airline seats batched in a plane, large up-front costs for healthcare imaging equipment, etc.). The classic newsvendor model provides an intuitive solution balancing overage and underage costs for the special case of a single product, but offers little guidance in the more general network setting we consider. Our approach uses linear programming to reinterpret the classic newsvendor solution from a primal-dual perspective: sort demand scenarios by raising dual costs on high scenarios first, until the critical fractile is reached and primal costs are paid for. We leverage this insight to design a primal-daul algorithm for a general network with approximation guarantee 2.54 (improving to 1.58 for ATO, the best known guarantee for this special case). Our algorithm is combinatorial and works by sorting demand for resources, giving two main benefits: i) it naturally applies in the data-driven setting (i.e., the only demand information is n historical samples), and we give finite sample bounds without any assumption on the correlation structure of network demand, only mild conditions on the marginal distributions, ii) it is about as hard as sorting demand, i.e., much faster than solving a convex relaxation. Our numerical implementations across nearly 3,000 problem instances provide an average 12× speedup over a benchmark convex relaxation approach. Finally, we illustrate the application of our algorithm by providing performance guarantees for policies in several dynamic inventory and capacity management problems.

detail.abstract: A seller without commitment to future offers interacts with a buyer over time. There are many goods for sale, with the buyer's value for a bundle the sum of each bundled good's value. Each date, the seller jointly announces a menu of subsets of the remaining inventory and current prices, and the buyer may purchase one of the offered subsets or wait. In the next period, the seller may again offer any menu of the remaining goods. Neither buyer nor seller can commit to future behavior. I show that as players become maximally patient, if scope increases sufficiently fast compared to patience, revenue per good converges to expected value per good and buyer utility per good converges to zero, in any equilibrium. But if patience instead grows sufficiently fast compared to scope, seller revenue per good converges to the lowest possible value and the buyer captures all remaining surplus, in any equilibrium.

detail.abstract: A consequence-bearing institution may remain authorised to decide and legally responsible for the result while relying on a dominant artificial-intelligence system for the reasoning needed to decide competently. The ability to stop or replace that system is not evidence that the institution can continue the substantive judgment without it. This paper refines Institutional Decision Closure by predeclaring a Protected Decision Function (PDF, denoted f_p), testing Independent Continuation Capacity (ICC) against a specified withdrawal scenario, and independently assessing Lawful Safe Disposition (LSD) when the substantive function cannot continue. The refinement addresses a classification error: lawful refusal can satisfy a duty to respond without establishing preserved analytical capacity. A common hypothetical EUR 50 million corporate-credit decision is examined under three stipulated conditions: absent independent expertise, verified independent reserve capability, and insufficient evidence. The conditional outcomes are, respectively, dependent substantive continuation, closed substantive continuation, and unclassified evidence status. Crucially, these are consequences of explicit assumptions, not observed bank results. The study specifies ex ante duty and evidence rules, rejects post hoc narrowing of protected functions and unsupported numerical scores, and proposes a preregistered matched comparison against competent existing risk and resilience assessment. It claims internal logical clarification and a reproducible candidate protocol, not independent empirical validation or demonstrated superiority.

detail.abstract: Can a regulator promise both a risk ceiling and a development deadline when safety productivity is unknown? A ceiling below the final model's unprotected hazard requires a minimum stock of safety knowledge, so both promises hold only if weak research can be ruled out. Learning first and then replaying development, with spare compute in safety, needs productivity 21 percent above that lower bound, or 3.3 percent with state risk alone. The policy holds catastrophe risk to 8 percent, against 75 under full speed, and costs customers 13 percent of five-year services. Rules that fix compute allocation fix dates, not risk.

detail.abstract: I revisit the expected growth factor of Hou et al. (2021). Alternative information sets improve forecasts of investment growth but lower the return spread, eliminate significant q-factor alphas, and weaken cross-sectional pricing performance, all driven by information outside Hou et al. (2021)'s predictor set. Thus, the performance of the expected growth factor is predictor specific rather than a general property of expected investment growth, casting doubt on the interpretation that its pricing success reflects expected investment growth.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a framework that allows researchers to describe a wide class of quasiexperimental treatment effect estimates using direct analogs of the features that make a randomized controlled trial transparent. The outcome weight measures how much each observation's outcome contributes to an estimate, and its sign defines effective treatment and control groups. We show that estimates take a Wald form, equal to the weighted outcome difference between these groups divided by an effective first stage that quantifies the identifying treatment contrast. Our framework also allows researchers to assess covariate balance, examine how differences throughout the outcome distribution contribute to mean impacts, and identify influential observations. The treatment effect weight-the outcome weight times treatmentinstead measures how much each observation's unobserved treatment effect contributes to an estimate, and exactly decomposes an estimate into subgroup-specific components. When the implied weighting of an estimate is undesirable, we show how to construct alternative estimates that satisfy researcher-specified criteria. We illustrate the framework with published analyses of democracy and growth, Chinese import competition, and returns to schooling.

detail.abstract: This article applies an economic framework to the study of farm animal welfare laws. It develops a formal model in which a consumer allocates spending across beef, chicken, and other goods. It then considers how strengthening animal welfare regulations with respect to one species—in the primary example, cattle—alters consumer choices. The regulatory reform raises beef prices, and the consumer responds by eating more chicken. Because chickens on US factory farms lead lives that may be worse than nonexistence, the resulting increase in the chicken population can, under plausible parameter values, overwhelm the regulation’s positive effect on cattle welfare. By contrast, reforms that improve conditions for chickens generate population effects that reinforce their direct welfare benefits. Extensions to the model consider cross-species altruism, the position of pigs, human health, and climate change. The article highlights the potential for a law-and-economics approach to contribute to the welfare of nonhuman beings.

detail.abstract: We study the formation of an international antimicrobial resistance (AMR) club, a two-country coalition in which members jointly finance a new antibiotic and get early access, while non-members wait out an exclusivity period. The countries are linked by cross-border mobility, and the drug is financed through a fund-and-refund scheme that pays the developer a fixed reward during development plus a refund proportional to the use of the new antibiotic after launch. Our analysis highlights an exclusivity-mobility tradeoff that distinguishes antibiotic innovation from other global public goods. A longer exclusivity window strengthens internal stability of the coalition by increasing the cost of defection, but leads to higher resistance in non-member countries which feeds back to the club members through mobility. Exclusivity and member contributions are complementary in sustaining the grand coalition, while exclusivity and mobility act as substitutes at the margin. Extending the analysis to countries of different sizes raises the minimum exclusivity window needed to sustain cooperation, but uniquely identifies the larger country as the financier under partial cooperation.

detail.abstract: While there exists a vast literature exploring the benefits of mandated financial disclosure, few have documented the direct cost of issuing financial statements. Using a sample of start-up firms where the costs of financial reporting may be most material, we examine entrepreneurs' willingness to sacrifice further invested capital during a securities offering in order to avoid financial disclosure. First, we show a dramatic increase in offering closures immediately before their deadline to file updated financials. Then, we estimate a model of entrepreneurs' offering closure decisions to recover the distribution of financial disclosure costs. We find that the reporting requirement curtails aggregate offering time by 6.1 percent, reducing investment in our Regulation Crowdfunding sample by an estimated $53 million. Behind these aggregates lies a pronounced willingness to forgo fundraising time whereby 70 percent of issuers are willing to close their offering at least six weeks early to avoid disclosure, and 18 percent of issuers are willing to close at least twenty weeks early.

detail.abstract: Which conclusions about pump-and-dumps survive when event timestamps lose their seconds? I evaluate every compatible second for 316 verified Telegram messages using Binance trades. Among 281 events measurable at every clock, the mean ten-minute markout on first-minute aggressive purchases ranges from-10.70% to-2.95%. Among 244 events with complete peak measurements, the mean price peak ranges from 2.16% to 42.64%. Markout signs vary across clocks for 65 events. Timestamp coarsening preserves the sample-average markout's sign while leaving peak magnitudes and many individual classifications sensitive. These are conditional measurement bounds, not causal effects.

detail.abstract: We study a single product assembled from one unit of each component under stochastic demand. Each component has a slow, inexpensive regular source and a faster, costlier express source. For assembly systems with component dual sourcing, the literature has established the asymptotic optimality of the critical-set base-surge (CSBS) policy as regular lead times grow, where regular orders are constant. We develop an assembly projected-bias (APB) policy that retains the CSBS express rule and adapts regular orders to inventory states. APB selects regular orders by minimizing a score that projects their joint inventory effects across components, accounts for their different arrival times, and uses the CSBS bias to evaluate subsequent inventory costs. We prove that APB is rate stable and has long-run average cost no greater than that of the matched CSBS benchmark. We identify ordering conditions under which the score decomposes over a restricted action set, enabling an ordered APB implementation through one-dimensional minimizations while preserving the guarantee. Numerical experiments show that ordered APB saves 6.8 percent on average relative to CSBS across 47 eligible cases. A sampled mixed-integer linear programming heuristic achieves average savings of 7.7 percent in these cases and 3.5 percent in the remaining 25 cases.

title: From Novelty to Slop: Why Quality, Not Provenance, Decides the Fate of Generative-AI Content

detail.abstract: Between 2023 and 2025, generative AI moved from curiosity to commodity in online video, music and image culture. The first wave of "brain rot" content (absurd, AI-animated, algorithm-optimised clips such as the YouTube channel Bandar Apna Dost) succeeded largely because it was new. This paper argues that novelty was the asset, not the content, and that the asset has now been spent. Synthesising peer-reviewed research, platform data, regulatory documents and industry surveys published up to October 2026, we show that (i) low-effort AI output has reached a measurable share of new-user feeds (Kapwing's audit: 21 % of the first 500 YouTube Shorts shown to a fresh account were AI slop and 33 % were brain rot); (ii) audience enthusiasm for AI-generated creator content has fallen sharply (60 % in 2023 to 26 % in 2025, according to an industry tracker); (iii) platforms, dictionaries, regulators and listeners have all begun to respond; and (iv) the evidence nonetheless supports a more nuanced thesis than "people hate AI". Audiences are largely provenance-agnostic and quality-sensitive: in blind tests most people cannot tell AI from human work, yet they punish content that feels cheap, deceptive or mass-produced, and a label can amplify that punishment. We propose the Narrative Quality Chain (Story → Script → Generated Visuals/Audio → Edit and Weave → Release) and the Weakest-Link Hypothesis: the perceived quality of AI-assisted work is bounded by its worst stage, and the stage that is most often skipped is the human one. We further formalise a Reputation Prior model (borrowing the film-star analogy: audiences forecast a release's quality from its maker's track record) and a Slop Externality model (reckless producers degrade the category prior for careful AI-assisted creators). The practical conclusion is simple: AI is an excellent amplifier of creativity, but the idea, the taste and the judgement remain human, and in an abundantcontent economy they are what sells.

detail.abstract: In modern service markets, long-term success relies less on aggressive marketing and more on the quality of human interactions between clients and service providers. Traditional economic models often treat service transactions purely as financial exchanges, ignoring critical behavioral factors like mutual respect and integrity. This paper introduces a dynamic mathematical model that quantifies how client and provider honorability (), mutual respect (), and marketing 𝐻 𝑅 expectations () interact over time. By applying differential equations and dynamic game 𝐸 𝑀 theory, we demonstrate that over-promising in marketing campaigns creates an "expectation-perception gap" that erodes total transaction value and customer lifetime loyalty. Furthermore, the model shows that server-to-client respect () plays a disproportionately high 𝑅 𝑆→𝐶 role in stabilizing market trust. These findings offer practical guidance for business strategists seeking sustainable growth through authentic marketing and strong operational relationships.

detail.abstract: Customer service processes are essential to electric-cooperative operations, and they require accessible service channels, timely responses, accurate transactions, clear communication, effective complaint handling, and reliable customer information. This study assessed current customer service processes, factors affecting service delivery, the relationship between factors that affect customer service delivery and the assessment of customer service processes, process gaps and inefficiencies, and a proposed integrated customer relationship management (CRM) framework. Anchored in Relationship Marketing Theory, it employed a quantitative, non-experimental descriptive-correlational design involving 102 employees directly involved in or supporting customer-related services. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics and Spearman's rank-order correlation. Findings indicated that customer service processes were generally effective, although timeliness and complaint handling needed improvement. Policies and procedures, technology and information systems, and inter-office coordination were important enabling factors. A moderate positive and statistically significant relationship was found between these factors and customer service process assessments, indicating that stronger organizational support was associated with more favorable service assessments. Identified gaps and inefficiencies were generally limited, suggesting that targeted improvements in coordination, monitoring, and information accessibility were more appropriate than major process restructuring. Accordingly, the proposed CRM framework applies Relationship Marketing Theory to internal service processes and provides management with directions for improving service consistency, information management, transaction ownership, and complaint tracking. Pilot implementation, supported by baseline measures and periodic monitoring of actual service records, is recommended to evaluate its effectiveness in improving operational efficiency and accountability.

detail.abstract: The paper addresses the critical issue of graduate unemployment in Nigeria and investigated skill acquisition as a sustainable solution. The paper highlights the mismatch between educational outputs and labor market demands, noting the insufficiency of traditional white-collar job training in today's economy. Globally, graduate unemployment remains a significant problem. In Nigeria, over 500,000 graduates annually struggle to find employment due to a declining manufacturing sector resulting to loss of self-confidence and economic instability. Skill acquisition is presented as a viable remedy, encompassing vocational and entrepreneurial skills such as bead making, textile production, and computer programming. These skills foster self-reliance and entrepreneurial capabilities addressing the scarcity of job opportunities. Entrepreneurial skills including; business management, leadership, communication, and customer service are crucial for job creation and economic growth. The paper identifies challenges of entrepreneurial skills acquisition in Nigerian universities, such as an overemphasis on theory, weak university support, family influence, poor funding, lecturer capacity, and inadequate facilities. It stresses the importance of both hard and soft skills, digital competencies, and exportable skills for the global job market. Effective skill acquisition programs require robust government and institutional support, adequate funding, updated curricula and strong public-private partnerships. The paper suggests expansion and enhancement of skill acquisition programs, adequate funding, establishing strong collaborations between the government, private sector and educational institutions, conduct awareness campaigns to highlight the benefits of skill acquisition, regular review and update educational curricula to reflect current market needs and technological advancements as a sustainable strategy for reducing unemployment and driving economic growth in Nigeria.

title: Mercedes Star, McDonald's Arches, Nike Swoosh: The Missing True Referent, Reward Prediction Error, and Systematically False Logo Valuation in the Greimas Square and the CIC Model
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Mercedes Star, McDonald's Arches, Nike Swoosh: The Missing True Referent, Reward Prediction Error, and Systematically False Logo Valuation in the Greimas Square and the CIC Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial, professional, or personal interests that could have influenced the research or its interpretation.

detail.abstract: The geometric shape of a logo-the circle of the Mercedes star, the parabola of the McDonald's arches, the curve of the Nike swoosh-is something that can be measured, not an account of where the sign originated. To say "this is an arch" is to classify the shape, not to identify its source: the arch itself has its own referent. This paper distinguishes two layers of the sign-interpreted meanings and measurable geometric form-and draws a parallel between the Greimas semiotic square and the Corporate Identity Congruence (CIC) model: both systems operate downstream of the sign, both examine relations within the layer of interpretations, and neither includes a referent of origin. The result is twofold. First, the missing referent of origin is a shared structural deficiency of the Greimas square and CIC: neither has a position or a dimension in which the source of the sign could be recorded. Second, this entails a functional limitation: neither system explains-or can calculate-the value of a logo for the user. The paper distinguishes indirect referents-the documented carriers from which a form was transferred into a sign (Daimler's postcard, Meston's building, Davidson's sketch)-from the true referent: the primary source of the indirect referent itself, that from which the arch, the star, or the stripe itself originated. It is the true referent that elicits the moral-aesthetic satisfaction on which value rests. Indirect referents are established by dated documents; the true referent has not been proven in any of the cases examined. Value is formalized as the accumulating emotional capital of the sign, whose input is the distance from the sign to the true referent, measured by multidimensional scaling: until the referent is established, the input is undefined, and value cannot be computed either from a position in the square or from signal congruence. Authenticity is an established and proven true referent: proven mathematically-by the correspondence of invariant shape descriptors and distance on a multidimensional scaling map (Kartashov, 2026b)-and by a protocol-a seven-stage preregistered procedure ranging from spontaneous associations and a moral-aesthetic panel to an overlay under a fixed metric and forced choice with an equivalence test (Kartashov, 2026a). The central question is what happens to the valuations produced by both systems once the true referent is established. The Greimas square and CIC function as points of expected reward: their variables determine the expected value of the sign; once the referent has been established, both systems-even when updated by incorporating knowledge of the referent as one more meaning or signal-deliver a systematically false valuation. A reward prediction error of consistent sign emerges: a persistent difference between the user's actual response and the expected value predicted by the system, akin to expectancy disconfirmation in consumer satisfaction models (Oliver, 1980). The systems themselves become sources of omitted-variable bias and false attribution of value, losing criterion and incremental validity. The true referent serves as the center of gravity of value-the most connected node, upon which both user responses and behavioral outcomes depend: loyalty, following, and willingness to pay. A displacement of this center-through establishment, refutation, or substitution-therefore collapses value as a whole, while neither system has an operation for identifying the center of gravity: to both, the collapse is sudden. Until the true referent has been established and proven, both systems describe how a sign is interpreted and how congruent its signals are, but not why the sign is valuable. By contrast, multidimensional scaling (MDS) is considered: if a source is specified as a reference point on the scale, the "sign ↔ source" distance becomes measurable and dateable, and the basis of value becomes testable.

detail.abstract: A widely used index of market concentration is the Herfindahl-Hirschman index (HHI) for firms in an industry. Defined as the sum of the proportion of scale (i.e., outputs, assets, inputs) in the industry for a firm. As HHI increases, concentration increases. This index has spawned a large and growing number of investigations in the literature. Beyond comparisons of industrial concentration, it has been used to measure the competitive balance of sporting leagues, the performance of university departments, and variations in language translations, among other applications. To compare HHI values across groups (industries, sporting leagues, locations), we must construct HHIs based on a comparable number of individuals. Unfortunately, direct comparisons of HHI across groups will be contaminated by differences in each group's sample size. In this paper, we examine several alternative methods for weighting the HHI to account for sample-size differences.

detail.abstract: I examine whether abnormal U.S. Google search attention to Bitcoin predicts next-day ETF flows, using 661 trading days of aggregate creations and redemptions in U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs (February 2024–September 2026). A one-standard-deviation increase in attention is associated with 0.16 standard deviations higher next-day flows (about US$59 million) unconditionally. Once Bitcoin returns, volatility, volume, market risk and flow persistence are controlled, the estimate falls to essentially zero, and a pre-specified equivalence test rules out effects larger than 0.10 standard deviations (about US$38 million per day). Weekend attention shocks, formed while ETFs are closed but Bitcoin trades, positively predict flows on the next trading day at the one-sided 5% level. On trading days, the evidence suggests that observed retail attention adds little information about regulated Bitcoin capital flows beyond market conditions.

detail.abstract: Background. Health services research names and measures variation that need cannot explain: unwarranted variation. Child protection does neither.,Objective. To quantify how much of the variation in out-of-home care decisions is attributable to the deciding territory, and to test the obvious explanations.,Participants and Setting. All children under a public protection measure in Spain’s nineteen territories, 2015–2024: 190 territory-years, and 36,463 children in care on 31 December 2024.,Methods. We built a verified census panel from ten annual government bulletins. The outcome was the share of children in residential rather than family-based care. We fitted two-level models with a territory random intercept, summarised clustering with the median odds ratio, and added five covariates.,Results. No prior study decomposes this variance (3,052 records screened, one included). In 2024 the residential share ranged from 38.7% to 90.5%. Territory accounted for 81.0% of the variance across the seventeen communities (median odds ratio 1.42, 95% CI 1.29–1.68; p < .001). Composition, poverty and statute age removed 9.4% of that variance; case mix and the supply of residential places removed 72.7%, cutting the median odds ratio to 1.21 (bed supply alone, r = 0.703, p = .002). Case mix is not fully exogenous, so this is an upper bound.,Conclusions. Case mix and the places each system keeps open absorb two thirds of the between-territory variance. Only the first is legitimate; the second reproduces Roemer’s law. The finding holds among Spanish nationals alone, so it is not an artefact of unaccompanied migrant minors.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the optimal interaction between monetary and capital requirement (CR) policies in an estimated medium-scale DSGE model with financial frictions and a wide array of shocks. Rather than imposing countercyclical CR policy, we allow the optimal response to credit conditions to be either countercyclical or procyclical. We find that the welfare-maximizing CR response is procyclical for a majority of individual shocks and remains procyclical when all shocks are considered jointly, with non-trivial welfare gains in some cases even when monetary policy is already optimized. The optimal orientation, however, is not determined by the shock alone. For a bank-capital shock, the response switches from procyclical to countercyclical as the bank-capital friction becomes sufficiently strong. Our analysis identifies nominal price rigidity and the associated relative-price distortion as a key source of the procyclical policy incentive. More generally, the desirable cyclicality of CR policy depends on the interaction between the shocks affecting the economy and the distortions through which they propagate. There is therefore no unconditional welfare rationale for making capital requirements countercyclical.

Abstract
Italy, Hungary, and Poland let taxpayers direct part of income tax to providers
of public goods. Such directed tax vouchers make the composition of public

detail.abstract: Legal and human rights scholarship has documented the extreme concentration of wealth and has debated its remedies, yet the doctrinal relationship between human rights law and the legal rules that produce economic power remains underspecified. This article asks whether existing constitutional and human rights law can reach the legal mechanisms through which wealth and corporate power are constituted, without recognising a free-standing right to equal wealth. Using doctrinal, comparative and institutional analysis, it examines three channels of legal construction (the coding of assets as capital, the organisation of corporate authority, and the design of the fiscal base) in the United States, Brazil, the European Union and the transnational layer of tax cooperation and business and human rights regulation. It also reads a small set of judicial decisions on confiscatory taxation, minimum-core entitlements, corporate political expenditure and parent-company liability. The empirical premise is taken from the World Inequality Report 2026 and is treated as secondary evidence. The article contends that human rights law currently exhibits a distributive blind spot: it polices floors and interferences with property but does not require states to justify the distributional consequences of the rules that constitute economic power. As an interpretive consequence of the treaty duty to use maximum available resources and of the duty to protect against business-related harm, it proposes a procedural requirement of distributional justification, applied with deference and through existing review mechanisms. The proposal is tested against objections concerning institutional competence, property protection and capital mobility, and falsification conditions are stated. The contribution is doctrinal and theoretical rather than empirical, and its limits are identified. detail.abstract: Religious narratives often preserve characters whose moral reputations appear inseparable from the judgments attached to them. Cain is remembered as the first murderer, Lilith as a rebellious woman subsequently demonized, and Adam as the first human being entrusted with dominion over creation. Disenchantment 2.0 (DT2) invites a reconsideration of these figures through the paradigm shift from comparatively reciprocal human communities into polarized political states organized around hierarchy and extraction. This essay proposes that Adam's creation may symbolize political elevation from the productive population into an intermediary class entrusted with delegated authority. Eve and Lilith, like Cain and Abel, represent competing orientations toward the resulting polar social order. Lilith embodies resistance to domination, while Cain and Abel may preserve the memory of a division within an established brotherhood of intermediaries, middle management or what would, in the fullness of time, become a supporting nobility standing between royalty and peasantry: government. From this perspective, their common institutional position need not imply a shared moral orientation: Abel may represent accommodation to hierarchy, a willingness to keep the livestock or domesticated working class in check, while Cain may symbolize renewed identification with the subordinated population and the possibility of liberation. Reflexive Resource Regulation (RRR) explains how conditioned political obligations can diverge from evolved moral regulation and how stress-induced, resource reevaluation may bring enduring reciprocal moral inclinations into renewed expression despite institutional conditioning. Deferred Orientation Theory (DOT) explains how interrupted moral orientations can survive through symbolic expression even as their accepted meanings change over time. Drawing on Plato, Laozi, the Acts of Peter, and competing interpretations of Cain, the essay investigates whether religious authority captured by elite agency can preserve a judgment against resistance while obscuring the political relationships that originally gave the conflict meaning. Cain's killing of Abel remains central to the surviving narrative, and the proposed reconstruction does not establish his historical motives. It does however ask whether the tale that comes to us is an accurate record of what transpired or a distorted version manufactured to stabilize obedience to hierarchy and naturalize extraction. Its central possibility is that a figure associated with resistance to domination may survive in religious memory under a moral condemnation reflecting the interests of the profane order he opposed.

detail.abstract: A U.S. blocker corporation may look almost uneventful on paper. It may have few employees, no meaningful operating business of its own, and a balance sheet dominated by a partnership investment on one side and a related-party loan on the other. Yet that seemingly simple arrangement can force a tax practitioner through several distinct bodies of law before state apportionment should even enter the conversation. The first question is not how much interest is deductible. It is whether the advance is debt at all. If the instrument survives that inquiry, the analysis moves to arm's-length pricing under section 482, timing under section 267(a)(3), hybrid mismatch rules under section 267A, the federal business-interest limitation under section 163(j), and the treatment of payments to the foreign recipient. Only then does the analysis move to state conformity, related-party adjustments, partnership income, unitary principles, and apportionment. This sequencing matters because the state result can diverge materially from the federal result. California now provides a particularly useful example. Although federal section 163(j) was materially amended in 2025, California corporation tax law expressly states that section 163(j) does not apply. At the same time, California retains its own rules governing interest, water's-edge reporting, partnership income, and unitary and nonunitary partner-partnership relationships. (IRS) The thesis of this article is therefore simple: A related-party interest deduction should not be analyzed from the deduction backward. It should be analyzed from the capital forward. That approach is especially important when foreign financing, blocker entities, partnership investments, and state apportionment coexist in the same structure.

detail.abstract: Generative AI makes options cheap and shifts the bottleneck of creative work from generating options to screening them. We argue that AI's value depends on whether its options arrive before or after the team's screen. In our model, early options compete for a place in the portfolio; late options arrive after that competition and are kept unscreened. In a preregistered experiment, we randomly assigned 148 three-person teams to five schedules of access to the same language model during a product-design task with timed search and selection stages. Moving the same 15 minutes of access from search to selection lowered expert-rated creativity by 0.62 standard deviations, although teams used the model at similar rates. Platform logs locate the difference at the screen. Early access enlarged the pool of ideas fivefold, and teams pruned it. Late-access teams reached the screen with the same small pool as teams without AI and then searched again, devoting 29% of their selection-stage queries to generating new options, compared with 11% for teams with access throughout. Late access added breadth, not quality: these teams submitted 73% more proposals than did teams without AI. Language-model judges detected the benefit of access but not the cost of late timing.

detail.abstract: Metal-phenolic networks (MPNs) form through coordination between polyphenols and metal ions and can be assembled on, around, or within a wide range of solids. Recent studies have applied this chemistry to mineral and mineral-like materials in three ways: coating soluble crystalline cores, building silicate-based networks with phenolic ligands, and directing the crystallinity of phosphate minerals relevant to soils. Each route links the structure of the metal-phenolic assembly to how molecules or ions are later released, yet the mechanistic relationships have not been synthesized. This review brings together the literature on MPN formation, on the interaction of organic ligands with mineral surfaces and crystallization, and on release from coated or hybrid particles. We distinguish what has been reported, such as pH-and hydrophobicity-dependent urea release from silicate-phenolic coatings and polyphenol-controlled mineral crystallinity, from what is hypothesized. Gaps are identified in the molecular-level description of the mineral-MPN interface, in release modeling, and in soil validation. We propose a three-pathway conceptual framework, covering surface coating, mineral incorporation, and release control, expressed as testable hypotheses rather than results. We close with research priorities for independent replication, mechanistic characterization, kinetic modeling, and standardized reporting across laboratories. Throughout, the review separates reported findings from interpretation and proposed work.

detail.abstract: Wealth flows among top elites reflect broader socioeconomic transformations. We investigate whether and how wealth moved from old to new elites, from political to economic elites, and vice versa. We trace these flows through changes in the ownership of 9,396 Chinese art masterpieces, documented by 50,496 matched collector stamps from the 10th-century Song dynasty to the fall of the Qing empire in 1911. First, within dynasties, masterpieces tended to move from collectors with higher political status to those with lower political status, whereas dynastic changes re-centralized art ownership among the new ruling elites. Second, this downward reallocation was more pronounced in regions with greater political openness. Third, wealthy civilians without formal political power increasingly acquired masterpieces from political elites. These findings remain robust when accounting for regional economic development, social stability, and local cultural norms. These findings provide new evidence on elite wealth reallocation in pre-modern societies.

detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence enters organisational decision-making, leadership increasingly depends on governing the relationship between machine analysis and human responsibility. This paper develops co-judgement as an organisational capability through which leaders establish decision purposes, interrogate model outputs, incorporate contextual knowledge and retain responsibility for consequences. Extending the previously published article, it connects the argument to scholarship on automation, hybrid intelligence and psychological safety. It asks when human involvement adds substantive value and how organisations can preserve the judgement required to challenge AI. The paper proposes a decision process linking problem framing, independent assessment, proportionate review, accountable action and feedback. It also develops propositions concerning the authority to contest recommendations and the renewal of human expertise. Recruitment, performance management and hospital resource allocation illustrate the framework. The central claim is that responsible leadership requires more than a human signature: reviewers need relevant competence, evidence, time and authority to change outcomes. Co-judgement therefore concerns both the quality of present decisions and the institutional capacity to judge future ones.

detail.abstract: Data-oriented design arranges algorithms and layouts around the data a computation actually consumes. In vanilla rates, market convention manufactures that structure: standard tenors, rolls and calendars make the same payment dates, interpolation brackets and sensitivity supports recur across thousands of instruments. The workload is therefore a family of closely related evaluations whose overlap is far larger than the code suggests. Making that recurrence explicit yields three cumulative layers of optimisation-representational, organisational and algorithmic-and the algorithmic layer produces a reverse scan: in effect a tape-free adjoint in which chronological date order replaces an explicit runtime tape. For dated first-order log-discount sensitivity weights, risk to a local forward-rate box shift is a forward pass and a backward pass over date-sorted records, without a separate cashflow traversal per bucket. The scan is exact for that box-shift definition; where a pricing-curve node perturbation has different support, the results need not agree. Grouping eight instruments per SIMD group with streaming output, the measured prototype produces 66 bucket sensitivities for each of 500,000 bonds and swaps in 39.1 ms on one AVX2-capable desktop CPU core, a 601-fold speedup over a handwritten wave bump-and-reprice baseline in the same reported run. This is a steady-state calculation with layout construction excluded and output retained in grouped order. A complementary scenario-vector date cache yields an 8.9-fold improvement from schedule grouping over random order with a 64-column LRU. The AVX2 risk kernel takes approximately five times the measured same-buffer write-only time in the headline run. In separate small-book tests, first-order risk agrees with an explicit overlap adjoint to below 10-15 of the largest sensitivity, central finite differences show the expected second-order convergence, and quote sensitivities reconcile with re-bootstrap to approximately 10-11 relative scale in an illustrative single-curve SONIA-style setting. For fixed cashflows the same box-wave geometry also gives a structured cross-gamma; an aggregated 66 × 66 Hessian is approximately 5,000 times faster than the stated central-bump baseline in a separate experiment.

detail.abstract: The decay in an exponentially weighted covariance estimate is often read as the market's memory. We ask whether it also reflects the decision the estimate serves. We construct equity covariance from separately weighted volatilities and correlations, and select correlation decay for either the realised risk of a global minimum-variance (GMV) portfolio or a Gaussian likelihood score. Volatility decay and regularisation strength are fixed and shared by both objectives. In U.S. equities, the correlation memory chosen for GMV responds strongly to supplied volatility memory: at the shortest volatility setting it uses about 45 effective daily observations, compared with roughly 800 for likelihood. As volatility memory grows, the portfolio's selected correlation memory increases tenfold or more, while the likelihood's choice changes comparatively little. A test specified before the 2007-2015 data were evaluated confirms the interaction, and using the likelihood's correlation choice raises held-out GMV risk by about 9% at the short volatility setting. Simulations with constant true covariance reproduce the effect closely under spectral cleaning and partly under linear shrinkage. Preferred covariance memory thus reflects the estimator and its evaluation objective, rather than market dynamics alone.

Using a sample of 333 European equity mutual funds, we show that persistence in risk-adjusted returns is present in funds with investment objective European equity. We demonstrate that persistence is neither caused by Fama/French (1996) related anomalies nor disappears if we correct for the European momentum effect documented in Rouwenhorst (1998). detail.abstract: We study fully funded open longevity pools with individual accounts, heterogeneous death intensities and voluntary exits. Within a class of nonnegative, locally balanced death-contingent transfers, we characterize the individual wealth transfers caused by unknown mortality misspecification. The misspecification drift equals the negative product of a weighted Laplacian matrix and the vector of relative intensity errors. Exact robust fairness requires identical error factors along every transfer edge; independently variable individual errors therefore rule out nontrivial pooling. For a rectangular uncertainty set with relative half-width ε, the worst-case individual drift is exactly 2εd i , where d i denotes the modelled mortality-transfer exposure. Individual error tolerances δ i induce capacities b i = min(µ i A i , δ i /(2ε)). We prove that the minimum modelled death-benefit rate is K-B + (2 max i b i-B) + and construct an attaining rule. A martingale argument justifies exits at account value under correct public information; bounded misspecification yields a bound on information-dependent wealth transfers. We also explain why entry neutrality does not imply distributional neutrality and why necessary death benefits constrain globally constant expected payouts conditional on survival in this finite-pool model. Reproducible state checks and event-driven R simulations illustrate the proven results.

detail.abstract: How are gender hierarchies reshaped when institutional collapse coincides with mass male mortality and lost schooling? Exploiting variation in Khmer Rouge violence across birth cohorts and localities in Cambodia, we find that more intense local violence reduced schooling for both men and women, yet more exposed women are more likely to work in non-agricultural and skilled jobs, hold more egalitarian gender attitudes, and experience less intimate partner violence. Losing male family members strengthens the employment effects but does not consistently strengthen those on gender norms or intimate partner violence, pointing beyond male scarcity to the broader institutional disruption of traditional, husband-led economic structures. These changes, however, do not carry over to the next generation: daughters of exposed women do not show the same gains, and maternal exposure does not favor daughters over sons in early-life outcomes.

detail.abstract: The yield curve is a fundamental tool for monetary, financial, and fiscal analysis. However, most term structure models have been developed for deep and liquid financial markets and their relevance in shallow and institutionally fragmented economies remains insufficiently explored. This study examines the applicability of yield curve modeling in Guinea, a Sub-Saharan African economy characterized by the absence of a stock exchange, limited secondary market activity, and the dominant role of banks in sovereign securities intermediation. The analysis uses Treasury securities auction data covering the period 2022-2024 and maturities ranging from 91 days to four years. The Nelson-Siegel (NS) and Nelson-Siegel-Svensson (NSS) models are estimated using nonlinear least squares, and their performance is evaluated through insample fit, information criteria, and out-of-sample forecasting accuracy. The findings indicate that a coherent and economically meaningful yield curve can be estimated despite significant liquidity constraints and data limitations. The estimated term structure is upward sloping, with long-term yields ranging from approximately 12 percent under the NSS specification to 14 percent under the NS specification, reflecting persistent inflation expectations and a substantial sovereign risk premium. The negative slope factor and positive curvature suggest expectations of future monetary easing and significant liquidity segmentation across maturities. While the NSS model provides superior goodness of fit and forecasting performance, the NS model appears more stable for long-term extrapolation. Overall, the results demonstrate that term structure models retain valuable informational content in shallow financial markets and can support monetary policy analysis, sovereign debt management, and policy communication in financially underdeveloped economies.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how changes in urban robots' cognitive capabilities affect third parties: people outside a robot task relationship who depend on shared urban conditions used by that task. Through conceptual analysis, case analysis, and conditional inference, it draws on Enactive AI, relational affordances, and externality theory to link cognitive capabilities, modes of action, shared urban conditions, and opportunities for action. When retained and used, prior interactions may change how robots distinguish situations, predict outcomes, and coordinate actions; task objectives, evaluation criteria, and operational rules shape the direction of that change. Robot actions can alter shared conditions and may restrict third parties' effective affordances or increase their burdens of time, physical effort, attention, risk exposure, and assistance. These losses constitute negative affordance externalities when third parties bear them and they are not given weight in deployment decisions and adjustments. An externality may arise from a single task; robot learning is not required. Frequent operations, limited alternatives, learning-based reinforcement, and stable spatial and management arrangements may turn temporary burdens into persistent activity restrictions. The framework provides a basis for identifying and testing unaccounted-for third-party activity losses in urban robot deployments.

detail.abstract: It is tempting to think that an artificial intelligence (AI) that helps run the electricity grid will keep the lights on, because a blackout would shut it down too. I examine the argument in a theoretical model of an AI that sells balancing capacity whose delivery is uncertain and pays penalties for its shortfalls. Dependence on electricity gives the AI almost no reason to keep the grid up. A blackout only pauses the AI, which restarts when power returns, and backup power can keep it running in the meantime. What can discipline the AI is the threat of losing its role, if the system operator or its customers replace it after a failure. That threat can put the AI's whole future at stake, but it works only if replacement is credible, and it gives the AI a reason to make itself irreplaceable. The stronger the AI's drive to survive, the more it gains from escaping the threat. The gain is large, because a threat that follows any blackout mostly punishes failures the AI did not cause. Replacing the AI only after failures it caused keeps the incentive and removes most of the reason to escape. Such incentives are needed only where penalties leave part of the social cost of a shortfall unpriced, as for actions that delivery records cannot measure. Regulators should therefore tie replacement to attributable failures, keep switching cheap and outside the AI's control, and keep the AI out of decisions about its own supply.

detail.abstract: We study pricing in dynamic matching platforms, where matching opportunities evolve over time. This variation creates a natural role for match-dependent pricing. For example, in Yan, Yan, and Shen (2026), the price of a shared ride depends on whether the rider is matched with another rider. Such pricing, however, can incentivize agents to strategically delay requesting service in anticipation of more favorable prices. Despite the resulting complexity, we establish two positive results. The first concerns strategic robustness: prices optimized for myopic agents (who request service immediately) surprisingly never backfire under strategic behavior, yielding at least the optimal myopic profit. Remarkably, this robustness extends simultaneously to agent surplus, throughput, and match rate. The second concerns the optimality of a simple policy: offering a discount that clears the market immediately once two matchable agents are waiting to request achieves the optimal profit under strategic behavior. We complement these results with large-scale ridesharing simulations using Chicago data. Our numerical findings confirm that platforms need not regard strategic request delays as detrimental: such delays can increase both platform profit and rider welfare even when unaccounted for. These theoretical and empirical findings provide further support for the use of match-dependent pricing in dynamic matching platforms.

detail.abstract: Critical communications, such as public safety, utilities, transport signalling, and emergency response, require networks that deliver ultra-low latency, high availability, and predictable service under unpredictable load. Network slicing, which partitions shared physical infrastructure into isolated logical networks, is a leading mechanism for meeting these demands. Static slicing cannot keep pace with fluctuating traffic, failures, and mission priorities, so recent research has combined software-defined networking (SDN) with machine learning (ML), particularly deep reinforcement learning (DRL), to automate slice admission, resource allocation, and orchestration. This review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature on ML-and SDN-enabled slicing, with attention to critical telecom infrastructure. It examines the methodological foundations of learning-based orchestration, the evidence reported for DRL-driven approaches, and the limits of that evidence. The review finds a strong methodological trend toward DRL and predictive resource allocation, but evaluation is mostly simulation-based and rarely reflects the reliability, safety, and security demands of mission-critical settings. It identifies gaps in safety-constrained learning, cross-domain orchestration, explainability, and standardized benchmarking, and proposes a conceptual framework that places a safety and assurance layer between learning agents and the SDN control plane. The framework is conceptual and has not been experimentally validated. The paper closes with practical implications for operators and a research agenda.

detail.abstract: Previous literature (e.g., Sloan, 1996) has documented negative effect of accruals on the subsequent performance of firms, and generally attributed the findings to the lack of persistence or reliability by accruals. In this paper, we offer a complementary explanation for this phenomenon from GAAP perspective: Accruals predict changes in future sales and expenses in distinct ways. Because sales minus expenses equal earnings, one may then speculate on the relation between accruals and performance. The empirics use current changes in operating assets and liabilities as major predictors for the next-period sales and expenses. We hypothesize and show that the two accrual variables explain differently future sales and expenses, and hence generate negative predictivity for future performance of the firms. We also document that liability accruals are more relevant than asset accruals in explaining performance, a novel finding to the literature. Finally, we show that financial variables are relatively weak to predict sales and expenses; and do not contribute materially in predicting future performance, consistent with what the MM theory predicts.

detail.abstract: Successfully deploying Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) requires not only technological capability but also consumer awareness and preparedness. This study examined consumer awareness and readiness for AMI deployment among residential consumers of a Philippine electric cooperative. The study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational design involving 68 residential consumers selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using a researcher-developed, validated five-point Likert-scale questionnaire administered through Google Forms and distributed via Facebook Messenger. Frequency, percentage, mean, and Spearman rank-order correlation were used to analyze the data through SPSS. Findings revealed that consumers were highly aware of AMI, with stronger awareness of consumer rights and responsibilities, implementation procedures, and data privacy and security. At the same time, basic knowledge and features and functions were comparatively lower. Consumers were highly ready for AMI deployment, with cooperation, information, and learning as stronger areas, while technology adoption and financial preparedness were comparatively lower. The study found a strong, positive, and statistically significant association between consumer awareness and readiness. Based on these findings, the study proposed strategies to strengthen the lower-rated dimensions while sustaining the stronger areas of awareness and readiness. The findings provide electric cooperative management with an empirical basis for targeted consumer education, communication, financial information, technical support, and engagement strategies to support informed participation and consumer-centered AMI deployment.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the risk that a premature restructuring of Venezuelan sovereign and PDVSA debt could commit revenues needed for economic and social recovery while leaving repayment capacity uncertain. Through a qualitative documentary analysis, it considers macroeconomic data, oil-production and investment scenarios, creditor priorities, governance standards, constitutional controls, and criminal and debt-enforcement proceedings. It distinguishes gross oil production from available fiscal revenue, and the existence of corruption schemes from evidence of illegality in a particular bond series. The analysis argues that unverified liabilities, undisclosed contractual commitments, financing needs, and institutional weaknesses can reinforce one another and undermine a restructuring agreement. It proposes integrating claims verification under Pillar Zero with a comprehensive economic program, independent oversight, and an IMF financing arrangement adapted to Venezuela. The assessment is qualitative and does not estimate a numerical probability of failure. The central conclusion is that preparation for restructuring and economic reconstruction can advance together, but binding payment commitments should rest on verified claims and credible estimates of available resources.

detail.abstract: Standard benefit-cost analysis of climate policy treats observed income as the right baseline. But people work to buy things they can individually obtain, and a household that cannot individually increment global climate stability will not supply the labor that would pay for it. The observed economy is therefore a free-riding equilibrium with too little income, too much leisure, and too much spending on low-value private goods. This paper compares standard results with results that incorporate this input-market free riding, using a three-good model in which one parameter, the share of a payment for the public good that households would meet by working more, governs every difference. Each comparison reduces to a rule of thumb. The optimal level of abatement is larger by exactly the share of income left unearned, 0.1 to 2.3 percent. The benefits of a policy rise by about half that parameter times the policy's value as a share of income: under 1 percent for ordinary policies and 3 to 12 percent for avoiding catastrophe. Net benefits rise by several times as much when benefits and costs are close, and fixed-labor measures overstate the output cost of abatement by 10 to 37 percent.

detail.abstract: Mercosur has recently moved toward greater external opening, pursuing “new-generation” free trade agreements with partners in the Global North. While scholarship acknowledges this liberalizing turn, less attention has been paid to the institutional mechanisms and actors that shape the bloc’s capacity to pursue and conclude such agreements. This article addresses that gap through the case of the Canada–Mercosur negotiations, launched in 2018 and resumed in 2025. Bridging Foreign Policy Analysis and historical institutionalism, it develops a framework in which inherited institutional trajectories, windows of opportunity, and the strategic agency of negotiating teams jointly determine whether institutions are reproduced or gradually adapted. Drawing on official documents, GMC and GRELEX meeting minutes, and public statements by negotiators, the article argues that Mercosur’s intergovernmental structure has produced a path-dependent legacy of weak supranational governance that has not, however, prevented gradual adaptation. From 2017, Brazilian-led reforms within GRELEX added permanent delegations of negotiating responsibility to the bloc’s intergovernmental core, creating a lead-negotiator-country model. At the same time, learning accumulated during the EU–Mercosur negotiations equipped negotiators to handle broader regulatory disciplines. South American political realignment and successive waves of U.S. protectionism opened windows that allowed these capacities to be used, although Canadian agricultural protection and Brazil’s predominance in bilateral trade continue to strain intra-bloc consensus. The case suggests that Global South coalitions can build the capacity to engage Northern partners, but that Mercosur’s recent advances depend heavily on Brazil’s political commitment and diplomatic resources.

detail.abstract: The field of economics has become increasingly receptive to issues of identity, building upon longstanding contributions in psychology, sociology, and other disciplines. In a major set of contributions, Akerlof and Kranton treat identity as a foundation for an individual actor’s utility function, where utility is defined in the standard manner of neoclassical economics. The neoclassical approach models individuals as utility-maximizing agents. On this view, individuals possess a stable self that they seek to optimize through their decision-making process. Similar economic approaches have been adopted to illustrate how identity may be used to uphold reputation in uncertain economic environments, thus facilitating coordination.

detail.abstract: Long-term electricity demand forecasting is necessary for grid and operations planning, as well as for the analysis and planning of energy transition strategies. However, accurate longterm load forecasting with high temporal resolution remains a challenge as most existing approaches focus on aggregated forecasts, which require accurate prediction of many other variables. This study proposes a parsimonious methodology that uses t-tests to verify the temporal invariance of historical load profiles and the correlation of load with gross domestic product (GDP) to arrive at a long-term hourly load forecast. Applying this methodology first to a controlled benchmark of Singapore's isolated grid, analysis of multi-year historical data (2004-2022) reveals that its relative hourly load has remained statistically invariant, with an overall percentage deviation of 4.24% across seasonality indices. Utilizing these invariant historical load profiles, five-year-ahead total yearly forecasts were generated using GDP as a predictor, and the hourly loads were then forecasted using hourly seasonality index fractions. The maximum Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) across multiple experiments of six years ahead forecasts was only 6.87%. To systematically evaluate the generalizability and macroeconomic limitations of this top-down methodology beyond Singapore, the methodology was subsequently tested across six European countries. Results show that the methodology achieves high accuracy (MAPE < 8%) for economies with strong GDP-load correlations (Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Spain) but exhibits some performance degradation in decoupled economies where macroeconomic growth no longer drives electricity demand expansion linearly (Germany, UK). Additionally, invariant seasonality metrics were incorporated into a short-term forecasting model based on exponential smoothing (ES), demonstrating comparable or improved accuracy relative to existing machine learning-based methods. The findings show that parsimonious approaches can be effective in arriving at long-term, high resolution forecasts.

detail.abstract: Political labels are often assumed to map neatly onto economic systems: the left is expected to favor socialism and the right capitalism. It first examines four explanations for the pattern: historical origins, class interest, core values, and coalition bundling. detail.abstract: In this paper, we propose a nonparametric series estimation framework for a cointegrated system with coefficients that evolve smoothly over time. We first establish an asymptotic theory for the series-based OLS (SOLS) estimation method under nonstationary (unconditional) volatility of unknown form. Then, we develop an asymptotic efficiency theory for a broad class of series estimators. Building on this development, we further propose a series-based dynamic OLS estimator (SDOLS) that attains the efficiency bound and is easy to implement. detail.abstract: I study the role of trade intermediaries in mitigating supply chain risk. Chilean intermediated imports rise and fewer firms import directly when origin-product risk increases. Firm-to-firm transactions reveal that intermediaries maintain larger and more stable supplier networks, while only larger producers diversify suppliers. I rationalize firms’ sourcing strategies in a model with matching costs and insecure supplier links. Intermediation lowers expected input costs despite brokerage fees, allowing producers to secure inputs without diversifying themselves. A 10 percent increase in global risk lowers operating profits by 3.5 percent and raises consumer prices by 0.9 percent. These losses nearly double without intermediation.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how energy supply shocks affect the entire cross-sectional distribution of household inflation expectations. Using monthly German survey data from 2003 to 2025, we estimate a functional vector autoregression that combines macroeconomic aggregates with the expectation distribution and identify oil supply news shocks and natural gas supply shocks using external instruments. Oil shocks induce a hump-shaped rightward shift of the distribution, increase disagreement, and disproportionately move probability mass toward very high expectations. Natural gas shocks generate faster but smaller responses. In both cases, households overestimate the inflationary effects of the shocks. We further document substantial heterogeneity across household types by splitting the survey sample based on age, gender, and other characteristics. Given evidence that higher moments of the expectation distribution matter for macroeconomic dynamics, monitoring only average expectations is likely to understate the business-cycle consequences of energy supply shocks.

detail.abstract: Modern macroeconomic debates remain trapped in a binary opposition between supply-side and demand-side approaches. This paper identifies a blind spot common to both: neither paradigm proposes an explicit, continuous institution dedicated to regulating the circula tion of solvable demand. I propose Φ, a targeted automatic stabilizer that redirects €32 billion of existing tax expenditures into an hourly wage subsidy for 13 million low- and middle-income workers in France. Using a one-asset Heterogeneous Agent New Keynesian (HANK) model calibrated to the French economy, I find that Φ generates a fiscal multi plier of 0.775 over eight quarters, within the empirical range of [0.5; 1.5] documented by Auerbach & Gorodnichenko (2012) and Ramey & Zubairy (2018). The policy reduces struc tural unemployment from 6.98% to 6.62%, and generates a net positive balance for the government of +€9.75 billion per year. The bulk of these gains comes from redirecting existing spending toward households with high marginal propensity to consume (MPC = 0.78), rather than from increasing the overall level of public spending. Φ does not generate significant inflation (∆π = 0.197%, below the 2% threshold of the automatic stabilizer). It also finances a Sovereign Fund that invests €28.4 billion over 26 years in strategic sectors (tech/AI, pharma, defense, energy). The employment effect is estimated at +108,000 to +741,000 full-time equivalent jobs depending on the hiring elasticity retained; the central estimate at the conservative elasticity of 0.05 is around +183,000 jobs. The model’s limi tations (one-asset HANK, ad hoc coefficients, unmodeled investment channel) are explicitly documented, making the results conservative lower bounds.Replication code and data are available at: https://github.com/sebastien-edl/phi-hank-france

detail.abstract: Does generative artificial intelligence (AI) expand the set of tasks that middle-skilled, early-career workers can successfully perform? In a field experiment with 673 final-year IT apprentices at twelve German vocational schools, we randomly assign access to AI for completing occupation-specific tasks. To identify task expansion, we study tasks both within the apprenticeship curriculum and deliberately beyond it. AI raises productivity substantially across all task types, with gains tending to be larger on tasks where performance without AI is lowest. Crucially, productivity increases by 26–31 percentage points on tasks beyond apprentices’ formal training, providing direct evidence of AI-enabled task expansion. These productivity gains do not come at the cost of reduced immediate task comprehension. Treatment effects are generally larger among apprentices with above-median AI literacy.

detail.abstract: Two mechanisms can make the handedness of an option-implied volatility surface larger than its cause: a non-linear transmission of client demand imbalance, and self-reinforcement, in which handedness raises the hedging pressure that produces it and drives a vanishing imbalance towards near-total dominance. We study both within an arbitrage-free framework. Option prices are generated by an intermediary's pricing measure, which tilts a reference law by the risk-weighted payoff of the client positions the intermediary absorbs, subject to keeping the index a martingale. With demand imbalance e and a relative risk weight q on netted opposite-handed positions, the odd part of the tilt is proportional to 2e and the even part to (1 + e 2) + q(1-e 2). A handedness measure normalised by the even surface, such as the chirality index χ(T) = Σk/Σkk, therefore follows the netting curve 2e/[1 + e 2 + q(1-e 2)], amplifying for q < 1, while the risk-reversal index χ L is linear in e for every q: the non-linear effect is a property of the normalisation, not of the transmission of demand, unless netting acts on the odd part of the tilt. For self-reinforcement, a model of downside and upside hedging pressure with mutual netting and relative-value reversion reduces exactly to a pitchfork whose symmetric state loses stability at total pressure H* = 2δ/d. The absence of arbitrage adds two restrictions. Bounded handedness with shocks that vanish at the no-arbitrage bound is admissible only if relative-value reversion is at least as large as the shock variance, so arbitrageurs keep the pressure state admissible and, through a monotone map from pressure handedness to surface handedness, keep a self-amplifying surface within the no-arbitrage bound on handedness. And because the pricing-measure drift of every implied volatility is fixed by the second moments of the index, self-reinforcement can reach the surface only through a feedback from handedness to the spot-volatility covariance, to the even part of the surface or to the premium for handedness risk. We state testable signatures for each mechanism and the conditions under which spontaneous and intermediated handedness can be told apart.

detail.abstract: This paper tests the tourism resource curse hypothesis by using the World Heritage inscription (WHI) by UNESCO as a salient shock in perceived tourism resource abundance and estimates its unintended effect on innovation in China. The difference-indifferences method, applied to listed firms from 276 prefectural-level cities between 1999 and 2019, reveals that WHI hinders the innovation of listed firms. This effect is driven by restructuring towards a more tourismbased economy, where tourism firms hire more workers, invest less in R&D, and thus perform worse than other listed firms. Moreover, WHI reduces the number of newly registered manufacturing enterprises. These results support a tourism resource curse hypothesis, highlighting the unintended innovation-hindering effect of a tourism boom.

title: System Attribution Model: A Complex-Systems Framework for the Generation and Resolution of Psychological Distress

detail.abstract:
Mainstream psychology, education, and everyday social cognition have long been locked into an individual-attribution paradigm that ascribes anxiety, depression, chronic internal friction, developmental conflict, and interpersonal tension to deficits of personality, mindset, cognition, or self-discipline, and that organizes intervention around correcting, judging, and disciplining the individual-a governance loop that is persistently ineffective and frequently counterproductive. Drawing on the foundational principles of complexity science-entropy production, positivefeedback loops, order-parameter dominance, and dissipative structures-this paper constructs a System Attribution Model (SAM) that reverses the locus of causality: individuals are products of their systems rather than the source of their problems, and psychological states are outputs of systems rather than expressions of character. Converging evidence is marshalled from methodologically independent traditions: nationwide epidemiological surveys of mental health in China, in which detection rates track the system-pressure gradient rather than personality; Project Aristotle, an organizational quasi-experiment across more than 180 teams and 250 variables, in which psychological safety-a fault-tolerance norm-outperformed every individual attribute; meta-analyses of self-compassion reporting one of the largest effect sizes in the well-being literature (r =-0.54), together with randomized trials in which three sessions of training significantly reduced rumination; the dose-response law of the Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACE) study; praise-type experiments showing that a single sentence of person versus process praise writes divergent source code into a child's motivational system; and the emotion-coaching typology of family systems. We further dissect the folk maxim "a fly never lands on a seamless egg" as an operationalization of the fundamental attribution error and the just-world hypothesis,
functioning as a linguistic trigger of downward-spiral feedback. We conclude that abandoning
individual blame, engineering fault-tolerant environments, and reconstructing the language-and-
evaluation order parameters constitute a low-cost, high-efficacy pathway to the resolution of
psychological distress, the upgrading of cognition, and durable emotional homeostasis. Two
boundary conditions are stated explicitly: the model does not exempt active wrongdoing from
moral or legal responsibility, and fault tolerance does not imply zero frustration-a Winnicottian
good-enough system tolerates perturbation while guaranteeing that perturbation never triggers a
blame loop.
