detail.abstract: We use two equity markets that share an identical prediction pipeline but differ sharply in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) as a natural experiment on a general machine-learning question: when does additional model capacity help a cross-sectional return predictor, and when does it not? For the United States (S&P 500, Sharadar data, 1996–2026) and India (Nifty 50, 1996–2026) we build point-in-time, survivorship-bias-free, sector-neutralised eight-feature panels and compare a linear model, gradient-boosted trees and a Transformer under purged, embargoed walk-forward validation. No model produces a significant out-of-sample information coefficient (IC) in the United States. India has a significant, economically tradeable signal (linear model: mean IC +0.051, Newey-West t = 4.96; net Sharpe 0.97 long-short, 0.79 long-only), but added capacity does not improve on it: the IC falls in point estimate at each step in complexity, although no model-to-model difference is individually significant. Four further experiments characterise this pattern. Continuous sweeps of tree depth and ensemble size show India’s IC is highest at the lowest-capacity settings, where a small tree ensemble matches the linear model. A positive control shows the models do recover injected non-linearity, but in India’s thin cross-section only at roughly two to four times the real signal’s strength. Resampling the US to India’s 43 names (800 draws) never reproduces India’s IC, ruling out a small-sample artefact. A synthetic (N × SNR) grid shows that under a linear ground truth added capacity hurts most at small N, India’s regime; the real markets’ own capacity effects, however, are measured too imprecisely to discriminate sharply between linear and non-linear ground truth. The evidence is consistent with the value of model expressiveness being governed by SNR and cross-section size, and identifies thin, low-SNR markets as a regime in which added capacity offers no benefit.

detail.abstract: This paper reviews and extends the literature on the costs and benefits of household debt relief. Debt relief transfers resources from creditors or taxpayers to debtors. This transfer can increase social welfare when households face incomplete markets. A lack of insurance against adverse events, such as job loss and illness, can be offset by the option to reduce debt payments. However, when debt relief imposes larger losses on creditors, possibly through borrower moral hazard, generous debt relief can reduce the supply of credit. Taxpayerfunded debt relief may also spur creditor moral hazard and inefficiently high lending if creditors do not fully internalize the cost of risky lending. Evidence for bankruptcy suggests that the insurance benefits outweigh the credit access costs. Through data and theory, I highlight parallels across different forms of debt relief that may guide future evaluations of optimal debt relief design.

detail.abstract: How much can dependence information improve the global protection of a fixed basket liability? With matching physical and pricing marginals, every financed additive hedge has the same unit mean. Under stated marginal conditions, minimum reserve fixes that payoff; excess reserve allows risk allocation. Four constituent puts approximate the full-class optimal risk with uniform absolute error O(ϵ^(3/2)) at small excess reserve ϵ, including zero dependence score. In a specified binary model with identical constituent marginals and basket laws, informative paired iid observations strictly improve risk at every positive excess reserve. We determine their exact finite-sample minimax value at a sufficient finite cap and, under a sufficient condition on risk aversion and available capital, solve sizing with both reserve budgets and training randomness.

detail.abstract: Cross-sectional momentum strategies rank assets by their past returns. This paper studies a different source of information, namely the way large price moves spread from one asset to another. I treat unusually large positive and negative returns as two types of events and model them with a multivariate Hawkes process, in which each event can raise the probability of later events in the same asset and in other assets. The fitted model is a directed network that separates an asset's own persistence from the influence of other assets. Using one-minute Binance spot data from 2020 to 2026 and a universe of the 50 most traded coins, selected each quarter without look-ahead, I evaluate the model in 22 out-of-sample quarters. Cross-asset excitation improves the out-of-sample fit in every quarter at the five-minute scale, and a placebo that breaks the timing between coins removes this gain. Large moves of either sign spread mainly from coins with heavy retail trading, such as XRP, DOGE and TRX, to large-cap and DeFi coins. A signed extension of the model, which captures the direction of transmission, predicts the cross-section of returns over 30 minutes to 4 hours after controlling for price momentum and for each coin's own events, and in this signed network Bitcoin is the clearest follower. Part of the effect at the shortest horizon is due to market microstructure, but the larger part remains when trades are delayed by one bar or priced at the next bar's VWAP.

detail.abstract: Why do insurance prices stay high for years after a shock? One answer is that risk-bearing capital is slow to arrive. I study grid operators paying mostly batteries to stand ready against blackouts, a new insurance market with observed capital, claims and demand. While Britain's new market lacked capital, expected claims were 2 to 6 percent of the premium; two-thirds was rent above claims and costs, lasting two years. Across eleven markets, premia fell by about half once capital caught up. Britain's listed insurers raised equity above net asset value, yet capital was slow because it had to be built.

detail.abstract: One of economists’ standard objections to rent control is that it reduces new housing construction, but the laws spreading today differ by design from the strict rent freezes that earned that objection. This paper extends Kholodilin’s (2024) review of empirical studies of rent control by coding each studied regime by its design features: how rent increases are capped, whether new construction is exempt, and what happens to rents between tenancies. Across these studies, rent control reliably lowers controlled rents, raises uncontrolled rents, lowers unit quality, and raises homeownership, but its effect on new construction and rental supply is not consistently negative. The particular design features a rent control law contains predict its effects better than either a generalized “rent control” label or the “generation” labels that have come after, and I propose coding on design features as a refined alternative to the conventional terms.

detail.abstract: Edge-of-field (EOF) practices installed at field borders to filter agricultural runoff are critical for improving water quality. Despite their effectiveness, adoption by farmers remains critically low. This study explores the influence of messengers on farmers' decisions to adopt EOF practices. We conducted an information treatment experiment using two information sources-an Extension professional and a farmer early adopter-versus a control group. Using an online survey of 373 Iowa farmer respondents in 2022, we built an empirical model to detect the treatment effect on farmer intention to adopt EOF practices. Our results reveal that farmers with less experience in conservation practices responded more positively to the treatments, and that a farmer messenger was more effective than an Extension professional in encouraging practice adoption. The farmer messenger increased adoption probability by 20.4 percentage points among respondents who are not currently enrolled in the Conservation Reserve Program, while the professional messenger yielded a statistically insignificant 7.7-percentage-point increase. Among respondents who decline adoption, both messengers reduced self-reported difficulty understanding how the practice works. These findings suggest that professional and peer messengers can each build technical understanding of EOF practices, while peer messengers are distinctively better at converting that understanding into stated intention to adopt. Outreach programs may therefore benefit from leveraging peer experiences and narratives, as farmer-to-farmer communication appears to resonate more effectively in these communities.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the predictive power and statistical significance of the Shiller CAPE ratio for 10-year forward real S&P 500 returns across 1,579 monthly observations spanning from 1881 to 2023. Consecutive 10-year forward return windows overlap by 119 out of 120 months, causing naive Ordinary Least Squares significance testing to treat heavily correlated observations as independent, overstating the significance of the CAPE-return relationship by approximately 6x. To address this, three significance tests were applied in escalating order of rigor: naive OLS, Newey-West heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent correction with 120 lags, and bootstrap permutation testing over 5,000 iterations. The CAPE-return relationship survives all tests, with the HAC-corrected z-statistic of -5.01 decreasing from a naive t-statistic of -24.302, a bootstrap p-value of below 0.0002, and the real coefficient being -0.00411. Out-of-sample predictive performance is evaluated using both expanding and rolling window validation, with Linear Regression achieving an average Out-of-Sample R² of 0.1417 excluding an anomalous 1991 fold, representing a 14% reduction in prediction error relative to a naive historical mean benchmark. Predictive power was found to be regime-dependent, exceeding an OOS-R² of 0.90 in historically low CAPE folds, and collapsing to -3.811 heading into periods of structural market change. A sequential Chow test with Bonferroni correction identifies a structural break from January 1979 to May 1991. Neither K-Nearest Neighbors nor Kernel Regression consistently outperforms Linear Regression, which supports an approximately linear relationship.

detail.abstract: Between 2006 and 2026 the European Union (EU) passed through four overlapping crisis waves: the financial and sovereign-debt crisis, the post-2014 Russia confrontation and the 2015 migration shock, the COVID-19 and Brexit disruption, and, since February 2022, the full-scale war in Ukraine. This paper examines the geopolitical dimension of that period using a small set of verifiable indicators: dependence on Russian energy, inflation and growth, defence expenditure, and forced migration. The central finding is a structural reversal. Russian pipeline gas fell from roughly 40% of EU pipeline imports in 2021 to about 6% in 2025, and Russia's share of extra-EU imports collapsed from 9.2% to 1.0%. In the same period EU defence expenditure nearly doubled, from €218 billion (2021) to €418 billion (2025). The paper argues that the EU absorbed the shock faster than most forecasts predicted, but at a cost in growth, industrial competitiveness and fiscal space, and that the next vulnerabilities are fragmentation of defence spending and new dependencies on the United States for LNG and security.

detail.abstract: This paper examines if RBI's FIT framework sustained inflation expectation anchoring during and after the 2022-2024 supply shock and if the tolerance band breach triggered measurable de-anchoring in Indian household expectations. Using bimonthly data from the RBI Inflation Expectations Survey of Households spanning September 2016 to November 2025, a sensitivity regression framework is employed across three sub-periods: pre-shock (2016-2021), shock (2022-2023), and post-shock (2024-2025) to test whether household inflation expectations became more sensitive to contemporaneous CPI during and after the tolerance band breach. Using first-differenced variables to address non-stationarity confirmed by Augmented Dickey-Fuller tests, the results reveal significant positive sensitivity of expectations to CPI changes during the pre-shock period, suggesting partial anchoring under FIT. During the 2022-2023 supply shock, CPI sensitivity becomes statistically insignificant across both horizons, indicating that changes in inflation did not drive expectation changes despite the tolerance band breach, consistent with forward-looking anchoring. The post-shock period shows near-zero insignificant sensitivity, confirming re-anchoring as inflation returned within the target band.

detail.abstract: Business upgrading programs in developing economies often generate substantial gains for male entrepreneurs but limited average impacts for women, raising concerns about both efficiency and equity. This study develops a Program Readiness Scorecard (PRS), a transparent, scalable tool based on 10 observable factors capturing both entrepreneurial resources and capabilities, to identify those most likely to benefit from such programs. Using pooled experimental data from firms in Uganda, South Africa, and Mexico, this paper shows that without targeting, firms led by men experience large and statistically significant gains, while those led by women have near zero average returns. Targeting that screens out entrepreneurs with the lowest scores on the PRS irrespective of gender improves women’s outcomes but leaves a significant gap. Applying a higher PRS threshold, specifically restricting eligibility to women in the top quartile of the PRS distribution, closes the gap entirely, as women with high scores achieve returns that are statistically indistinguishable from men’s. These results are robust to multiple sensitivity checks. The findings have two broad policy implications. First, targeting based on the PRS can strengthen program outcomes for women-led firms while also identifying the cohort in need of remedial support prior to joining high-value initiatives. Second, beyond gender-focused programs, the PRS can be applied in a wider range of settings where scarce program resources must be directed toward enterprises with the greatest potential for sustained growth.

detail.abstract: A NATO member since 1952 and host to the İncirlik air base-one of the Alliance's most strategic installations in the Middle East-, Turkey has simultaneously established itself as the most active NATO partner of the Russia-China-Iran axis: the purchase of the Russian S-400 airdefense system, the Akkuyu nuclear plant built by Rosatom, the TurkStream gas corridor, participation alongside Moscow and Tehran in the Astana format on the Syrian file, the coupling of its Middle Corridor with China's Belt and Road, and repeated bids for BRICS membership, for which it obtained "partner country" status in 2024. This article sets out to analyze this strategic balancing act and asks the following question: does Ankara's ambivalent diplomacy stem from a sincere commitment to impartiality in the service of peace, or is it above all a structural survival strategy designed to prevent Turkey from becoming the target of either camp? Drawing on the literature on hedging and the strategic autonomy of middle powers, as well as on the most recent developments-the interception, in March 2026, of an Iranian ballistic missile by NATO air defenses over Turkish territory; the persistent freeze, since 2019, of the F-35 file despite Ankara's repeated calls for an easing of CAATSA sanctions; the reaffirmation, in early 2026, of Turkish BRICS ambitions despite its NATO membership-, the article advances a twofold thesis. On one hand, Article 5 of the Washington Treaty functions as a shield that deters anyone from directly attacking Turkey, since doing so would amount to attacking the entire Atlantic Alliance; this shield grants Ankara room for maneuver that non-allied states do not enjoy. On the other hand, Turkey's geographic position-control of the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles under 1 the Montreux Convention, status as NATO's second-largest army, lock on the Alliance's southern flank, and energy hub between Europe, Russia, the Caucasus and the Middle East-makes its continued anchoring in the Western camp just as indispensable to NATO as access to its good offices is for Moscow, Beijing and Tehran. The result is neither disinterested neutrality nor opportunistic double-dealing in the pejorative sense of the term, but a rational strategicautonomy policy, made possible by a geographic and institutional irreplaceability that neither camp can afford to sacrifice.

detail.abstract: The IS•LM framework describes short-run equilibrium through the interaction of the goods market and the money market. The IS curve represents combinations of output and the interest rate at which planned expenditure equals output, while the LM curve represents combinations consistent with money-market equilibrium. This paper presents a parameterized IS•LM simulation implemented in Wolfram Mathematica/Wolfram Cloud. It outlines the model structure, discusses comparative-static predictions and selected literature, presents the supplied code and graphs, and uses screenshots of the simulation interface as descriptive evidence of the displayed model configuration. The screenshots document a particular state of the model but do not independently establish causal effects. The interpretation of the plotted money-market line requires attention to the equation and axis conventions, because the standard linear LM relationship is upward sloping in income-interest-rate space when money demand is increasing in income and decreasing in the interest rate.

detail.abstract: This paper is the third in the Built Environment Series, after The Walls We Choose and The Seal and the Silence. In Ontario, most new condominiums are financed by selling them before they are built. Lenders typically expect about 70 percent of units to be pre-sold before they release a construction loan, and the federal capital rules for banks reward pre-sales only when the buyer's contract is binding and the deposit is forfeited if the buyer leaves. This paper follows an invented household, labelled as such, from a pre-sale signed in 2021 to a closing in 2026 at which the appraisal falls far short of the contract price, and sets its story beside documented cases: buyers facing closing gaps of $120,000 and $595,000, a court award against a buyer who could not close, and private mortgages whose fees and renewals multiply the debt. It reviews evidence linking mortgage arrears and financial strain to depression, skipped meals and medication, and heart disease, and notes that no study has followed pre-sale buyers through the months before closing. It argues that the structure places the price risk of a five-year project on the party least able to carry it. As an alternative, it proposes a second model for the Canadian Affordable Housing Trust: resident building groups, adapted from the German Baugemeinschaft, in which future residents build at cost for themselves, supported by seed loans, a construction-loan guarantee and a pooled reserve, and by six legal changes that require no Crown land. It closes by following the same household through a building group, where the risk is shared, visible and chosen.

title: Subjective and Temporal Quality-of-Life Information in Bayesian Networks
affiliations: Radboud University and Radboud University

detail.title: Subjective and Temporal Quality-of-Life Information in Bayesian Networks
detail.abstract: In clinical decision support systems, Bayesian networks are often preferred as formalism for learning and reasoning with causally related information. As white-box AI models they combine domain expertise and data in stochastic causal models that allow for transparent, robust, and explainable inferences, like the best fitting treatment or follow-up of cancer patients. To facilitate personalized healthcare, the models require both medical and quality-of-life aspects. A major challenge with quality-of-life information is that it is inherentlysubjective and ordinal; we are typically interested in change rather than absolute value; e.g., a treatment that slows down a decreasing quality-of-life. One needs to reason with subjective, but ordered and temporal information (”I’m feeling better today than yesterday”). This implies novel representations, learning algorithms, and inference approaches of such informationin Bayesian networks. In this paper we propose such a representation and demonstrate, using a simple case study with synthetic data, how stochastic variables based on subjective (but ordered) temporal information can be learned and how prognostic and diagnostic posterior inferences can be made.

detail.abstract: This report examines Americans’ views of retirement security using findings from the National Institute on Retirement Security’s (NIRS) national public opinion survey. The findings reveal growing concerns about retirement preparedness, with 80 percent of Americans believing the nation faces a retirement crisis and 68 percent saying that preparing for retirement is becoming more difficult. Inflation, debt, rising living costs, and uncertainty about Social Security are among the major concerns. The report also identifies significant gaps in Americans’ understanding of retirement savings and income needs, continued support for traditional pensions, and widespread agreement that policymakers should place greater priority on retirement security. In addition, it explores Americans’ attitudes toward artificial intelligence and alternative investments in retirement plans. Together, the findings highlight the financial challenges facing Americans as they prepare for retirement and the growing public demand for solutions that strengthen retirement security.

detail.abstract: Weather-index microinsurance is an effective instrument to the management of agricultural risks in smallholder farmers yet the retention of policyholders is a big problem. This paper evaluates policyholder churn in weather-index microinsurance by incorporating the traditional insurance functions, transaction footprints, and basis-risk indicators in an econometric and machine-learning model. The empirical study is grounded on 250 observers of policyholders which include 106 policyholders who are churned and 144 policyholders who are retained. The distribution of financial, transactional, demographic, environmental and insurance-related variables are analyzed using descriptive statistics. Econometric benchmark of logistic regression and machine-learning model of Random Forest are applied. According to the descriptive results, the household income was used to determine the average monthly earnings to be 243.12 with an average of 14.28 transactions using mobile money. The basis risk was severe in 11.20% of the observations and parametric payouts were activated in 28.80% of the observations. The logistic regression model had a ROC-AUC of 0.6515 and the Random Forest model had a ROC-AUC of 0.5606. The coefficient of Severe_Basis_Risk was positive and statistically significant (β = 1.9161, p = 0.001), while the coefficient of Monthly_Income_USD was negative and statistically significant (β =-0.0051, p = 0.009) in the logistic regression model. These results show that exposure to basis-risk and household financial factors include predictive information related to policy lapse in the future among the sample studied. But, the results of the analysis at hand lack enough evidence on which to base an incremental predictive value of transactional footprints data or data on basis-risk indicators extra to the rest of the explanatory variables. The results indicate the possible usefulness of the synthesis of descriptive statistics, econometric modelling, and machine-learning methods to study the phenomenon of policyholder churn and also underline the significance of high-quality validation and recognition of how predictive association does not imply causal inference.

detail.abstract:
Foreword: The idea of associating a monetary value with human life is very challenging and
can seem insensitive or harsh. Life is indeed priceless, at least when considered from
the complex perspective of an individual. However, policy makers are regularly devising
policies and regulations that affect people’s risk of death and that seek to protect lives
in society, and require methodologies for comparing the costs of reducing risk with the
expected benefits in terms of lives saved. The analysis presented in this report will help
policy makers get a better measure of such benefits.
The report takes stock of surveys from around the world where people have been asked
about their willingness to pay for a small reduction in mortality risk, and analyses the
variation in the estimates resulting from differences in study designs (including the way
risk changes are displayed), characteristics of risk (type and size of risk changes, baseline
risks, etc.), socio-economic characteristics (age, income, gender, health status, etc.), and
other variables.
The report offers guidance on how the findings of the analysis can be included in
future assessments of policies that affect mortality risks. Such assessments will need to
take into account the income level in the given country, as well as characteristics of the risk
change in question and the population affected by it. Such guidance will help to improve
the information base upon which important decisions are taken on mortality risks faced
by society.

The report was published as "OECD (2012), Mortality Risk Valuation in Environment, Health and Transport Policies, OECD Publishing." Prepared by Henrik Lindhjem, Ståle Navrud, Nils Axel Braathen and Vincent Biausque

title: Distribution Is the Primordial Tacit Pact Reinforcing the Origins of Distribution Economics: An Intellectual History of the Exit Concealment and Return of Distribution
affiliations: KBRI(Korea Barbecue Research & Institute

detail.title: Distribution Is the Primordial Tacit Pact Reinforcing the Origins of Distribution Economics: An Intellectual History of the Exit Concealment and Return of Distribution

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: none
declarations.funderStatement: none

keywords: The Primordial Tacit Pact ( 의 太初 默約

detail.abstract:
Distribution is “the Primordial Tacit Pact ( 太 初 의 默 約 ).” This one sentence is both the conclusion and the starting point of this paper.
Distribution was the beginning of the economy. Classical economics, too, took distribution as the central task of political economy. Yet what became the skeleton of modern economics was production, labor and wages. This paper traces, from four angles, how this inversion came about.
In the history of ideas, distribution was banished to the realm of politics and absorbed into the theory of production. Ethically, labor became a virtue, and the system of measurement counted only production. Anthropologically, distribution became, together with the granary, the secret of power. In political philosophy, modern power escaped responsibility for distribution by erasing the face of the distributor. At the bottom of all this lies the logic of accumulation. Production can promise tomorrow without naming any losers, but distribution must name its losers now. Capital is deferred distribution turned into matter.
The paper then defines the age in which AI replaces labor as the age of legitimation, in which the return of distribution is unavoidable. At the same time, it warns of the danger that this return may regress into premodern distribution of the bestowal (下賜) or benefaction (施惠) type. It distinguishes four forms of distribution: bestowal, benefaction, contract and co-sharing (共分). It shows how distribution came to be regarded as something for nothing and as begging, points out that the law has treated distribution not as a right but as a reflex benefit, and argues that distribution is not a favor, but a right. It then presents a five-layered principle of consolidation that makes distribution irreversible.
Finally, the paper redefines the origin of distribution not as sharing before the hearth, but as the silent consent given before setting out to hunt and gather, that is, an unspoken promise concerning the dignity of mutual survival. It names this layer the Primordial Tacit Pact, Pactum Tacitum Primordiale. Distribution is not the result of production but the condition that precedes production; the hearth is the expression of distribution, and the Primordial Tacit Pact is its substance. The paper then presents, as the counterpart to the three factors of production, the Four Elements of Distribution: Dignity ( 尊嚴), Endurance ( 堪耐), Participation ( 參與) and Contribution (寄與). The factors of production rely on what can be priced. The elements of distribution are rooted in what cannot be priced, namely the sublimity of mutual survival.
This argument serves as a reinforcement that provides an originary foundation for the income system and institutions presented in Distribution Economics.

detail.abstract: The growth of Islamic finance in Africa depends not only on market demand but also on the strength of legal, regulatory, institutional, and infrastructure frameworks. This study assesses the readiness of ten selected beneficiary countries of the Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa (BADEA) to support Islamic finance. The study selected five countries from each of the four regions: Eastern and Southern Africa and Western and Central Africa. The author developed a structured nine-dimensional readiness framework. It covers: legal and statutory arrangements, prudential and supervisory frameworks, tax and accounting treatment, Shariah governance and certification, liquidity and market infrastructure, capital markets and Sukuk, Takaful and pension systems, consumer protection and financial inclusion, and human capital and institutional capacity. Each dimension is scored on a 0-4 scale and weighted based on its institutional importance. The weighted scores are combined into a Composite Readiness Score and converted to a 0-100 scale. This readiness index provides a comparative indication of the extent to which each country has the conditions required for broader Islamic-finance development. The results show wide variation in readiness, from 43.1 in Rwanda to 93.8 in Nigeria. Nigeria and Senegal are classified as High; Kenya, Tanzania and Niger as Moderate-High; Uganda, Ethiopia, Ghana and Mali as Moderate; and Rwanda as Low. The study contributes an integrated, transparent framework for Islamic-finance readiness across multiple institutional dimensions, and evidence for sequencing of Islamic-finance initiatives in BADEA beneficiary countries.

detail.abstract: A firm that wants innovation must attract workers whose suitability for exploration it cannot observe. Any contract that attracts explorers is also open to exploiters. In a two-period model with hidden actions, explorers and exploiters generate different performance histories. The firm therefore screens by placing pay on histories relatively more likely under the intended activity than under mimicry, so the timing and path dependence of compensation become instruments of selection. Exploiters are paid for each success; explorers mainly for long-run success and, only when early failure is sufficiently diagnostic, after early failure. Commitment, termination, and feedback screen by the same logic. A common contract can help overcome a lack of commitment; separate contracts earn their keep when termination or feedback must differ. Two predictions follow. Exploration-oriented incentives change who enters, remains in, and chooses exploratory work, not merely innovative output. Competition for talent shifts where pay sits across histories, not merely its level.

detail.abstract: This paper presents the Mechanism of Rates equation, a modified Taylor-type rule with interest-rate smoothing that maps the prior policy rate and five publicly observable macroeconomic variables-core PCE inflation, the unemployment gap, the 10-year/2-year Treasury spread, the monthly change in WTI crude oil, and the monthly change in the Federal Reserve's balance sheet-into a suggested federal funds target midpoint. Using real-time data, we evaluate the equation at the eight FOMC meetings of 2025 and, new in this version, at the September 2026 meeting, which is a true out-of-sample test because the coefficients were fixed in March 2026. Across 2025 the model's mean absolute error is 0.23 percentage points (RMSE 0.25), seven of eight predictions fall within ±0.30 pp of the realized rate, and the model carries an upward bias of 0.15 pp; it does not, however, outperform a naive no-change benchmark (MAE 0.09 pp). At the September 2026 meeting, where the FOMC raised the target range by 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%, the model pointed in the correct direction but overshot: it produced 5.63% from raw inputs and 4.68% after applying the ±8% oil cap, against a realized midpoint of 3.875%. The overshoot reflects inputs-notably a 23.9% one-month oil surge and 3.3% core inflation-that lie outside the "good-market" ranges for which the equation was designed. We conclude that the equation is best used as a transparent policy-gap indicator rather than a point forecast, and we propose step-limited and regime-aware extensions.

detail.abstract: Background: Temperature exposure is often represented by mean temperature, but averaging maximum and minimum can alter categorical thermal extremes. We assessed whether representation changes classification across scales and estimands.Methods: We analysed governed CHIRTS-ERA5 monthly Tmax and Tmin data for Kenya nationally in 1990–2024 and across all 47 counties in 2000–2024. Tmean was derived as (Tmax+Tmin)/2; Full Max–Min retained both endpoints. Fixed five-class thresholds, derived from Hansen’s 1951–1980 climate-dice classification convention, defined Hot and Very Hot as the warm tail. Representation contrasts used paired circular annual block bootstrap inference with 10 000 replicates and 3-, 5-, and 7-year blocks. Holm adjustment was applied to class-specific contrasts. For binary switching, Full Max–Min was the priori criterion and Tmean the test representation; McNemar tests complemented bootstrap inference.Findings: Nationally, the five-class discrepancy was not statistically distinguishable (D=0·0502; p=0·1884), but endpoint-weighted Hot+Very Hot was 5·83 percentage points higher under Tmean than Full Max–Min (38·81% vs 32·98%; p=0·0127). At county level, the discrepancy was larger (D=0·0803; p<0·0001), with an 8·97-point warm-tail difference (p<0·0001). Against Full Max–Min, county Tmean classification had 67·14% sensitivity, 98·96% specificity, 79·48% concordance, and 20·52% switching. McNemar tests showed strongly asymmetric discordance.Interpretation: Temperature representation is a measurement decision, not merely preprocessing. Averaging can suppress endpoint-defined warm states, particularly elevated minimum-temperature conditions, and can alter the hazard signal delivered to climate-health surveillance, preparedness, and adaptation planning and response.Funding: This study received no specific funding from any public, commercial, or not-for-profit organisation.

detail.abstract: We study whether financial markets shape firms' pricing behavior and, through this channel, the transmission of macroeconomic shocks into inflation. We develop a novel measure of firm-product markup premiums using granular retail scanner data that isolates firms' pricing decisions from common demand and cost shocks and applies consistently to public and private firms. We show that exposure to public markets changes pricing behavior: firms increase markup premiums following an IPO, and public firms raise markups and consumer prices significantly more than matched private firms during the 2021-2022 inflation surge, contributing roughly one percentage point to cumulative inflation. These differences are strongest among firms facing greater investor pressure and stronger equity-based managerial incentives. A Bayesian learning model rationalizes these patterns through the information and incentives generated by public markets. Our findings highlight a new channel through which financial markets may amplify inflation.

detail.abstract: This study examines the causal impact of rental prices on fertility in Germany, a housing market characterized by low homeownership rates and substantial regional variation in tenure structure. Using a county-level panel from 2011 to 2019 and an instrumental variable approach based on residential construction permits, we estimate the elasticity of fertility with respect to rental prices. A 1% increase in rental prices reduces fertility by approximately 0.66%. When accounting for local homeownership shares, the negative relationship is significantly attenuated, although fertility declines remain present across all regions. The magnitude of the decline is smaller in counties with higher ownership rates. Age-specific results indicate that fertility among women above age 30 is more responsive to rental price changes, and the moderating effect of homeownership is stronger for this group. Robustness checks across alternative ownership thresholds and expanding sample windows confirm the stability of the findings. Overall, housing market structure shapes aggregate demographic responses to price shocks.

detail.abstract: Purpose. Consequential records are often reviewed after the fact by people who did not participate in the original decision. Their ability to assess the decision depends on whether the record preserves enough information to reconstruct its basis. This study examines whether a structured, record-level documentation quality read can identify differences in that reconstructability. Design/methodology/approach. A three-level read, Ready, Needs work or Gap, was applied to 32 publicly available public-records cases from 32 distinct sources across four document classes and two states, issued between 2005 and 2026. The read and a contemporaneous note explaining its basis were recorded from the source before the documented outcome was consulted. Ten cases were independently re-read. Findings. The read corresponded with independent government audit findings in all five cases where comparable audit assessments were available. It was associated with reconstructability as reflected in contemporaneous basis notes: six of seven noted Needs work cases recorded that the basis could not be rebuilt, compared with none of 17 noted Ready cases (p = 0.0000520). The read also distinguished document classes according to the extent to which the underlying basis was exposed (p = 0.00466). It was not associated with appellate outcome in the resolved subset (p = 1.000), consistent with reconstructability and appellate disposition representing different properties. Research limitations/implications. The corpus is small, non-random and limited to two jurisdictions. Reliability evidence is preliminary because only 10 cases received an independent blind re-read. Practical implications. The findings suggest that reconstructability can be examined at the record level before a consequential record is finalised. A structured review that records both the assessment and its basis may provide an additional mechanism for identifying documentation weaknesses before records are subject to later audit, review or challenge. Originality/value. The study provides an initial empirical examination of a structured record-level approach to assessing whether the basis for a consequential decision remains independently reconstructable from the record itself.

detail.abstract: Governments hold long-term renewable support contracts signed when costs were high, and from 2027 the European Union will require two-way contracts for difference (CfDs) or equivalent schemes for new support. Can a government and a generator both gain by voluntarily rewriting one? I show that the answer depends on which of two gaps a deal exploits. Generators discount future cash more heavily than the state, which rewards paying them early. An upfront buyout of part of the strike price creates surplus. Generators also value fixed revenue above market revenue, which makes longer contracts valuable as insurance. The common trade of a lower price for a longer contract combines a costly deferral with this insurance and works only when generators' premium for market risk is large. Using Britain's public contract data, I calibrate the model to seven legacy offshore wind contracts that pay £168-221 per megawatt-hour against £95 in the latest auction. Buying their strike prices down to that level creates £0.8-1.1 billion of surplus, depending on the government's discount rate. Price-for-length swaps fail at central estimates and need a larger premium, generators' rates near the state's or high market prices. Governments should pay early and sell insurance separately.

detail.abstract: Constitutional courts increasingly decide corruption-related disputes, yet comparative scholarship tends to treat transparency, accountability and integrity as interchangeable goods and to examine anti-corruption law mainly as criminal policy. This article asks how constitutional adjudication in democratic systems relates transparency, accountability and public integrity to the limits of public power, and whether those limits operate on the corrupt use of office alone or also on the machinery built to repress it. Using doctrinal and comparative legal analysis, it examines seven decisions from four jurisdictions: the South African Constitutional Court's decisions in Glenister (2011) and Economic Freedom Fighters (2016); the Indian Supreme Court's electoral bonds judgment (2024); the Brazilian Supreme Federal Tribunal's rulings on corporate campaign donations (ADI 4650, 2015) and on the retroactivity of the 2021 improbity reform (Theme 1199); and the United States Supreme Court's decisions in McDonnell (2016) and Snyder (2024), read against the United Nations Convention against Corruption. The argument is interpretive and normative, not empirical. It proposes that transparency is best understood as an input to accountability rather than a substitute for it, and that constitutional democracies bind public power in two directions: against officials who convert office into private advantage, and against enforcement authority that outruns legal clarity, independence or proportion. The article derives three adjudicative conditions from the comparison, identifies where the thesis could fail, and states the limits of its evidence base.

detail.abstract:
Background: Living donor kidney transplantation is declining in Brazil and elsewhere, and the payer responsible is unknown. We decomposed the decline by funding source.

Methods: We conducted an ecological time-series study of Brazil, 2008–2025, using country-year as the unit of analysis and the public share of living donor transplantation as the primary outcome. We identified publicly funded transplants in national hospital admission microdata and the all-payer total in the Brazilian Transplant Registry; the difference estimated private-sector activity. We estimated trends by Prais-Winsten regression on each log series.

Findings: Neither the public share of all kidney transplants (82·2–88·9%; p = 0·38) nor the deceased donor share showed a trend. For living donors, it fell from 79·9% to 71·0% (annual percent change −0·94%; 95% CI −1·19 to −0·70; p < 0·0001). Both sectors lost volume: the public from 1429 to 606 transplants (−6·26%; p = 0·00027), the private from 359 to 247 (−2·36%; p = 0·064), a significant difference (ratio −4·35%; −5·50 to −3·18; p < 0·0001). Of 935 living donor transplants lost, 823 (88·0%) were public; living donors fell from 45·5% to 10·6% of publicly funded transplants, a program that grew 82·5%. The waiting list rose from 19,440 to 38,925 and deaths on it from 1215 to 2906 (2015–2025).

Interpretation: Living donor kidney transplantation in Brazil contracted, driven largely by the public sector, as the public program expanded and demand outgrew supply. What was lost is the only modality independent of deceased donors.

detail.abstract: This paper covers Oregon's recent passage of SB 608 in 2019, a softer modern rent control that caps the annual rent increases at seven percent on top of an allowance for inflation, makes an exception for new builds which remain free from rent control for their first fifteen years, and allows rents to adjust to the market rate between tenancies. I use parcel-year assessor records on both the Oregon and Washington sides of their shared border in a difference-in-differences design, and I find no aggregate decline in new construction. To find a proxy for rental construction, I use new builds on the parcels held by absentee owners; I estimate these fell by roughly 1.2 per 1,000 parcels relative to those on the Washington side of the border. However, these estimates are attenuated by the existence of only one clean post-treatment year in these data and a contaminating pre-treatment differential trend.

detail.abstract: The Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962, the confrontation surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and tensions at Bab el-Mandeb in 2026, together with the possibility of a Chinese quarantine of Taiwan, call for a reassessment of maritime coercion. These situations are neither identical nor legally interchangeable. In Cuba, the United States sought to prevent the arrival of additional Soviet weapons. At Hormuz, pressure on Iranian trade intersects with contested maritime passage. At Bab el-Mandeb, attacks, selective restrictions and coastal fighting notably involve a non-state armed group. Around Taiwan, a quarantine remains a prospective scenario. This article argues that controlling flows can secure concessions without immediate conquest, but its effectiveness depends on alternative routes, third-party responses and the management of escalation. The analysis distinguishes the law governing recourse to force from the rules applicable to naval warfare and shows that disruption at several chokepoints can increase the vulnerability of African economies. It concludes by proposing that maritime security, port connectivity and continental integration be considered components of African strategic autonomy.

detail.abstract: High-performance computing (HPC) and large-scale data-intensive workloads increasingly rely on cloud infrastructure, where tens of thousands to millions of virtual machines must be coordinated in near real-time. Existing cloud load balancing and data staging solutions require manual backend pool enumeration, external orchestrators, and decoupled storage configuration-approaches that do not scale seamlessly and introduce significant configuration latency, operational overhead, and state drift. In this paper, we propose a novel Subnet-Level Automatic Load Balancing and Data Partitioning Architecture that eliminates manual configuration by anchoring server discovery, dynamic traffic routing, and dataset staging directly to the fundamental structural boundaries of a cloud Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) subnet. The proposed system designates one or more IP addresses within a subnet CIDR block as load balancer endpoints, autonomously discovers healthy backend servers across the remaining IP space via periodic non-intrusive health sweeps, and dynamically routes incoming Layer-4/Layer-7 requests accordingly. A complementary data distribution subsystem partitions heterogeneous datasets (binary, JSON, XML, YAML, CSV, archives) across all active nodes according to configurable capacity weights. We provide formal mathematical models, multi-load-balancer horizontal scaling algorithms, fault tolerance mechanisms, and practical cloud control-plane integration strategies. The proposed architecture substantially reduces provisioning time, eliminates operational bottlenecks, and serves as an autonomous networking primitive for next-generation cloud and HPC environments.

detail.abstract: Almost exactly two years ago COVID-19 spread to the United States. Following the federalism model, the 50 states and their governors and legislators made many of their own pandemic policy choices to mitigate the damage from the virus. States learned from one another over time about what policies worked most and least effectively in terms of containing the virus while minimizing the negative effects of lockdown strategies on businesses and children.This study is an expanded and updated version of an October 2020 report card of how pandemic health, economy, and policy varied across the 50 states and the District of Columbia (Committee to Unleash Prosperity 2020). It examines three variables: health outcomes, economic performance throughout the pandemic, and impact on education.

detail.abstract: This paper studies personalized pricing for a good with positive consumption externalities and heterogeneous consumer influence. A monopolist uses data to identify and offer targeted discounts to high-influence consumers, but low-influence consumers can masquerade as highinfluence types at a cost. Manipulation contaminates influence data, misallocates discounts, and weakens the aggregate-demand feedback generated by influential consumers. Sufficiently high manipulation costs can therefore raise both firm profit and aggregate consumer surplus relative to costless manipulation. When data coverage is endogenous, the firm may exercise strategic data restraint because broader data use increases the return to imitation. Price commitment turns manipulation decisions from strategic substitutes into strategic complements. It can deter manipulation, but its profitability relative to responsive pricing depends on equilibrium selection.

detail.abstract: These trends highlight the need for a deeper evaluation of how wage policies intersect with broader economic factors, such as inflation and currency depreciation, to influence workers' real incomes. This study examined the effect minimum wage adjustment on workers purchasing power. The sample size of 203 was arrived at using Slovin formula. The study adopted purchasing power theory of wages as the theoretical framework. Descriptive survey design enabled the description of the current state of wage adjustments and data were generated from mixed-method approach which combines qualitative interviews and quantitative data generated from questionnaire. Quantitative responses obtained from the Questionnaire were analyzed by descriptive statistic while qualitative data obtained through interview were analyzed thematically. Findings from this research reveal that wage adjustment has slightly improve the living condition of some workers at the beginning but get worse of later on and failed to improve their financial and economic wellbeing. This is due to inequity, inflation and devaluation of currency that eroded the purchasing power of workers salaries. Therefore, workers are not satisfied with their current wages and demand for regular review to meet expectation. Therefore, the study recommends regular and inflation response wage review, link wage adjustments to cost-of-living index, addressing pay equity between staff and stabilizing macroeconomic environment should be in the forefront.

detail.abstract: This study examines household liquid-savings allocation under stylized multi-currency cash-flow scenarios using historical Kazakhstan exchange-rate data. Daily USD/KZT and EUR/KZT exchange-rate data are used to generate joint scenarios with a dependence-preserving stationary bootstrap. The household profiles are synthetic and are designed to isolate different forms of income-expenditure currency mismatch rather than to represent observed household behavior in Kazakhstan. Synthetic household profiles with different income-expenditure currency mismatches are evaluated over one, three, and five-year horizons. Savings weights in KZT, USD, and EUR are selected by minimizing the 95% Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR95) of cumulative expenditure shortfalls. FX-exposed profiles with an all-KZT boundary achieved the lowest CVaR under the baseline specification. It was shown that the minimum CVaR95 was 1.1872 for the USDincome and KZT-expense profile and 0.5083 for the fully multi-currency profile at a three-year horizon. According to reported benchmark and robustness comparisons, expensematched savings outperform the income-matched portfolio. The expense-matched portfolio with a fully multi-currency profile showed CVaR only 4.7% above the minimum, while the income-matched portfolio was 23.6% above. Therefore, the main conclusion is that not every household should hold exactly 100% KZT, but household savings should be primarily held in the expense currencies to cover essential costs.

detail.abstract: The explosion in the use of Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) credit products has revolutionised the market for consumer credit due to their capacity to enable consumers to split their payments over short-term periods, typically interest-free, at the time of purchase. While BNPL credit products are often positioned as a low-risk option compared to credit card products, there is increasing evidence drawn from a variety of secondary sources that the combination of structural features of the product, lack of regulation, and consumer behaviour renders BNPL credit products similar to debt traps for financially vulnerable consumers. The current paper presents a synthesis of research evidence from government reports, peer-reviewed journal articles, and institutional data sources, generally dating from 2013 to 2026, on the mechanisms through which BNPL credit use leads to overspending and loan stacking. Narrative systematic review methodology informed by inclusion and exclusion criteria is employed using PubMed, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and institutional sources such as the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) and the Federal Reserve System. Findings show that usage of BNPL is prevalent among younger individuals and those who are poor and have bad credit; that installment payments decrease the significance of spending through processes explained by mental accounting and hyperbolic discounting theory; and that there is a correlation between BNPL usage and increased credit card debt, personal loan debt, late payment fees, and likelihood of suffering from depression, anxiety, and posttraumatic stress. The paper discusses how BNPL can offer some advantages, such as cash flow management and interest-free loans for unbanked consumers, and reviews regulatory responses to BNPL in the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Europe, and India. The paper finds that BNPL is not all negative nor all positive, but that the risks of BNPL usage are disproportionately borne by the most vulnerable consumers.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how hurricane risk affects public procurement outcomes using Texas Department of Transportation auctions from 2000-2013. Hurricane exposure is associated with fewer plan holders and bidders and with higher bids. We estimate a procurement auction model with constant absolute risk aversion (CARA) preferences and selective entry. The model estimates an average residual contractor loss of 6.2% of the engineer's cost estimate (ECE) when a hurricane strikes. The implied hurricane premium is 1.05% of the winning bid, and compensation for bearing risk is 1.56 times the expected hurricane cost. Actuarially fair full insurance reduces winning bids in exposed auctions by 0.59 percentage points of ECE on average (about $30.0 million a year, since larger contracts save more); restoring the plan holders deterred by hurricane exposure reduces them by 0.13 percentage points. Holding participation fixed, risk aversion itself lowers procurement costs: risk-neutral bidding would raise the median winning bid by 7.81 percentage points of ECE, because risk-averse bidders compete more aggressively.

detail.abstract:
This aimed at examining the nuenced effect of interest rate volatility on economic growth in Uganda using annual time-series data covering the period of 1993 to 2024. The research employed a quantitative approach. Secondary data was extracted from the bank of Uganda (The interest rates variables that is Lending rates, Deposit rates, Rediscount rates, short and longterm treasury bills) and world bank. The analysis focused on the key monetary policy instruments, including but not limited to volatility in; lending rates, Treasury bill rates (shortterm and long-term), and the rediscount rate, together with other selected macroeconomic variables such as investment, Consumption and Financial Deepening index. Generalized Least Squares (GLS) regression techniques were employed. The findings showed that investment has a strong, positive effect on economic growth in Uganda across all models, underscoring its importance in expanding productive capacity and supporting long-term development. 

Second, the results on Interest rate volatility were mixed. Volatility in lending rates, deposit rate, short-term and long-term Treasury bill rates negatively and significantly affects economic growth, suggesting a high transmission of volatility in the financial markets to the real economy. However, volatility in the rediscount rate has a positive and statistically significant effect on economic growth. This implies that active monetary policy interventions by the Central Bank of Uganda (BOU), particularly those influencing long-term liquidity conditions, may support economic activity during periods of adjustment. Finaly, the study concludes that economic growth in Uganda is driven more by real sector factors, especially investment and that financial market volatilities negatively affect growth. The researcher recommends the need for disciplined monetary policy, effective liquidity management, and sustained investment promotion to support stable and inclusive economic growth in Uganda.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a two-state consumption-based asset-pricing framework that compares model-implied risk premiums and valuation measures under favorable (good) and unfavorable (bad) economic conditions. The Mathematica implementation defines separate functions for good-state and bad-state risk premiums and prices, alongside risk-free-rate functions. Principal inputs are expected consumption growth, the standard deviation of consumption growth, a time-preference parameter, and the externally specified probability of the bad state. The good-state probability is defined residually as one minus the bad-state probability. The paper interprets the model in relation to equilibrium asset pricing, the equity premium puzzle, present-value valuation, and cyclical variation in risk compensation. The supplied plots are comparative-static illustrations rather than empirical estimates. An algebraic inspection shows that the two risk-free-rate functions as currently coded simplify to the same expression, 1/delta, and therefore do not vary with state probabilities. The paper recommends clarifying parameter units, validating the state-specific expressions, and distinguishing the current two-state comparative-static framework from a fully specified econometric state-space model. Empirical estimation and out-of-sample testing would be required before making claims about predictive performance.

detail.abstract:
This article examines the intersections between the Data Act and the Artificial Intelligence Act, using a selection of research activities of a public institution in the field of hydraulic engineering as an example. In particular, it focuses on data access rights, the use and generation of such data in AI system development, and requirements for data quality, interoperability, risk management and documentation obligations. Finally, the article discusses the provisions that govern compliance monitoring. In summary, the essay concludes that public research institutions should bear in mind both regulations when developing AI systems, particularly if they are to be used operationally at a later stage. 


The interplay between the two regulations is important, since they address different priorities yet together ensure access to high-quality data for developing AI systems is possible and of the utmost importance. In order to maximise the effectiveness of the regulations, research institutions should consider them when making key development decisions during the research phase. This will also ensure that the transition to operational use is not hindered by a lack of compliance.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether Barberà and Gerber’s framework of games of addition can provide a formal basis for analyzing organizational decision-making and whether it eliminates the need for the distinct mathematical treatment of the internal operations of hierarchical organizations envisaged by Oskar Morgenstern in the RAND Corporation’s RM-734 report, entitled Prolegomena to a Theory of Organization. Building on a generative-grammar formalization of Morgenstern’s proposal, it compares two sources of structure in organizational decision processes: preference-sensitive strategic interaction and the generative effects of delegation, signaling, and resource deployment. Games of addition extend sequential game theory by allowing the identity of the actors initiating subsequent actions and the possible orders of play to emerge endogenously through strategic interaction and equilibrium conditions, making them suitable for organizational processes in which several actors may be able to initiate subsequent actions. However, this game-theoretic framework does not by itself explain how the underlying space of organizational possibilities is generated and constrained through historically constituted competence structures, resource-deployment outcomes, and other contextual conditions. The paper therefore distinguishes strategic choice within a decision structure from the generation or transformation of that structure and proposes a complementary analytical approach in which competence structures generate the space of feasible organizational trajectories while games of addition analyze strategic interaction within that space. The analysis supports the complementary application of both formal frameworks to the analysis of organizational decision-making rather than the substitution of one for the other.

detail.abstract:
How much of the defense premium that appears around geopolitical shocks reflects
exposure to defense contracts, and how much reflects the fact that defense contractors are low-
beta? I study six events in the 2025–2026 Iran Conflict using 70 U.S.-listed firms over 491
trading days, of which 47 have defense contract revenue and 23 have none. Defense exposure is
measured from Federal procurement records. The paper reports two results. The substantive one
is a sign reversal: the cross-sectional correlation between defense exposure and same-day
abnormal returns is +0.53 on 13 June 2025, when Israel struck Iran, and -0.51 on 24 June 2025,
when the United States struck and a ceasefire was announced; the difference is significant under
a paired bootstrap over firms (p < 0.001) and is not matched by any other eleven-day pair in the
sample (randomization inference p = 0.081). Read as a group difference, firms with defense
contracts outperformed firms with none by +1.78 percentage points on 13 June and
underperformed them by 2.08 points on 24 June; roughly a third of that spread reflects the fact
that defense contractors are low-beta and technology firms are high-beta, and after adjusting for
each firm's own beta the spread narrows to +1.13 and -1.44 points while remaining significant. A
formal result underlies the decomposition. Because the market return is common to all firms on a
given day, subtracting it is a location shift and leaves every cross-sectional statistic exactly
unchanged: firm-level market adjustment cannot remove market-wide variation from a cross-sectional event study, and the adjustment must be firm-specific to do so. The methodological
finding is that this is nearly all that survives. None of the four event-window mean abnormal
returns is statistically significant, and the largest of them, +0.66% on 13 June (t = 1.81), has a
randomization-inference p-value of 0.62: days producing cross-sectional averages that large are
common. The two approaches disagree because they treat different units as the sample — firms
or days — and the treatment in an event study varies at the level of the day. Across a family of
29 reported tests, false-discovery-rate control leaves three results standing at 5%. The paper's
contribution is as much the demonstration as the finding: in a small event study, the choice of
sampling unit determines whether a result exists.

affiliations: Columbia University

detail.title: Housing Market Segmentation and Monetary Policy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the research reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: The author gratefully acknowledges financial support from Columbia University through the Anna J. Schwartz Fellowship.

detail.abstract: Recent evidence shows that contractionary monetary policy raises U.S. housing rents even as house prices fall. I argue that this response reflects a shift in housing demand toward renting in segmented markets: tighter credit raises the cost of owning for constrained households, and because converting housing to rental use is costly, rental supply cannot expand enough to absorb the added demand, so rents rise. I quantify this mechanism in a New Keynesian model estimated on 1975-2019 U.S. data and disciplined jointly by the rent response to monetary policy and the slope of the tenure-supply curve. Tightening monetary policy in response to rising rents can reinforce the shift toward renting, and thus rental pressure. Excluding shelter from the target improves welfare, and a re-optimized rule with a stronger response to goods inflation improves it further. A stabilization objective that places most weight on goods inflation selects nearly the same rule. Additional responses to rents or house prices add little.

title: Reducing Mean Time to Resolution with Open Telemetry: A Framework for Correlated, Vendor-Neutral Observability
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Reducing Mean Time to Resolution with Open Telemetry: A Framework for Correlated, Vendor-Neutral Observability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NO FUND
declarations.funderStatement: NONE, Self investment

detail.abstract: As enterprise systems decompose into microservices running on dynamic infrastructure, the time required to restore service after an incident is increasingly dominated not by the fix itself but by the search for where and why the failure occurred. Telemetry is typically abundant but fragmented across vendor-specific agents, inconsistent naming and disconnected stores for metrics, logs and traces, so that responders must correlate signals manually under time pressure. OpenTelemetry, a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation project formed from the merger of OpenTracing and OpenCensus, provides vendor-neutral APIs, SDKs, a wire protocol (OTLP), a collector and semantic conventions that together enable consistently described, correlated telemetry. This paper analyzes how OpenTelemetry reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR). We decompose MTTR into detection, acknowledgement, diagnosis, mitigation and verification phases and argue, drawing on incident studies, that diagnosis is the dominant and most variable phase in distributed systems. We present a reference architecture for OpenTelemetry-based observability and identify six mechanisms-context propagation, shared resource identity, signal correlation through trace identifiers and exemplars, semantic conventions, collectorbased enrichment and sampling, and service-level objective alerting on derived metrics-and map each to the phases it shortens. We evaluate the framework on three modeled incident scenarios and show how phase-level improvements compound into MTTR reductions, while being explicit about the statistical weaknesses of MTTR as a metric. We close with implementation guidelines, a maturity model and a discussion of limitations and future directions including continuous profiling and AI-assisted diagnosis.

detail.abstract: Symbolic regression finds the formula that best predicts an outcome, so under endogeneity it returns a formula for the conditional mean, not the structural law. This paper scores the formula search with instrumental-variable moment conditions instead: candidate formulas from cheap generators are refitted by GMM on sieve instruments, selected by a GMM model-selection criterion with a structure penalty, and reported with an Anderson-Rubin confidence set over formulas that says whether the data identify the result. The selection rule is consistent for any generator whose candidates contain the true form, with a finite-sample bound that attributes its failures to weak separation or to fitting moment noise, and the confidence set covers the true form without any rank condition. In a Monte Carlo over five designs and five laws, the method recovers the log, power and two-regressor laws in 92-100% of runs under confounding and a heteroskedastic first stage, while the squared-error search never recovers the power law under strong endogeneity, and it flags every weak-instrument run as weakly identified or rejected. On the Engel curves of the 1995 Family Expenditure Survey it reproduces the known Working-Leser and quadratic shapes; on Angrist and Krueger's quarter-of-birth instruments it reports weak identification instead of a formula.

detail.abstract:
The erosion of the dollar-centric order is habitually framed as a search for a substitute currency: which unit — the renminbi, a digital asset, a basket — will take the dollar's place. This paper rejects the framing. The action is not in the currency layer but in the settlement layer. The operative question is not what one pays with, but whether value needs to cross the border at all. Reciprocal trade can be discharged by offset, and once it is, the cross-border payment disappears as an event. The paper names this shift the settlement turn.

Two independent forces compress cross-border transfer. The first is sanctions-driven and highly visible. The second is de-risking: correspondent banking relationships have contracted by roughly a quarter between 2011 and 2020 on CPMI data, with flows concentrating in fewer institutions and emerging and small economies losing direct links. The paper deliberately separates these forces, because conflating them makes the argument look geopolitical when it is in fact structural.

The argument rests on a suppressed lineage: Milhaud's interwar campaign for multilateral offset, Keynes's International Clearing Union with its unit of account, and the European Payments Union of 1950–1958. The Special Drawing Right is read as the de-fanged descendant of that lineage — the unit of account survived, the clearing function did not. From this lineage the paper reconstructs a typology of settlement fallback across a two-tier sample — seven core multilateral arrangements and five contrast cases: netting is not an exotic alternative but the regime to which an economy reverts whenever monetary settlement is constrained.

Two binding constraints follow. The first is the multilateral-netting problem inherited from the transferable ruble: unless net positions are fungible across partners through a common clearing house, a nominally multilateral scheme collapses into bilateral balancing. The second the paper reframes as the compliance paradox of netting. Anti-money-laundering and sanctions regimes are engineered for gross, transaction-level monitoring; netting internalizes and aggregates, so the screenable transaction dissolves. The claim is scoped: the blindness of transaction-level supervision to offset is known from the literature on informal value-transfer systems as a marker of illicit channels, and in market clearing it was addressed by moving supervision to the participant level. The paper treats it as a structural property of any netting arrangement, including a legitimate multilateral one, and explains why transplanting the market-clearing solution into trade clearing is non-trivial.

The paper differentiates its argument from weaponized interdependence, from the currency-centric de-dollarization literature, and from multi-CBDC bridges. On the last point the empirical record is instructive: after the BIS exited Project mBridge in October 2024, the platform continued under five central banks, with the digital renminbi accounting for the overwhelming share of settlement volume. A bridge optimizes the transfer and, where flows are asymmetric, encodes that asymmetry; a clearing house removes most transfers through offset. The layers are complementary, not identical.

Normatively, the paper proposes a multilateral netting-clearing scheme (NCS) with compliance-by-design and recasts the central counterparty as a compliance institution screening at the gross-obligation stage, before netting. It closes on the agency available to an intermediary state that institutionalizes a clearing node as a supervised, auditable arrangement rather than a gray corridor. The Operational Toolkit is a diagnostic profile of six criteria for assessing the viability and legitimacy of a proposed scheme.

detail.abstract: GLP-1 usage has fundamentally altered the foods that consumers buy and are sold through retail stores. In this paper, we study the strategic effects of food manufacturers' responses to GLP-1-driven changes in consumption. detail.abstract: On 29 September 2026 the White House Accord on Super Intelligence committed the six largest American AI developers to engage an "independent external auditor" without defining who may hold that role. The ensuing debate in Washington has opposed two candidates: the nonprofit evaluation organisations that grew out of the AI safety movement, and the large American consulting networks. This paper argues that neither satisfies the independence requirements that the assurance profession has applied to itself since Sarbanes-Oxley, and that the question is not new. Assurance on subject matter other than financial statements is governed by an existing international standard (ISAE 3000 Revised), an existing code of independence (IESBA) and existing regimes of public oversight (PCAOB, H2A, FRC). What is missing is not a framework but an auditor: a statutory auditor, free of advisory relationships with the auditee, subject to public oversight, and-this is the paper's central claimestablished outside the auditee's own jurisdiction. We derive six eligibility criteria from the financial-audit precedent, show that they are symmetric (an American auditor for European developers, a European auditor for American ones) and therefore politically acceptable on both sides of the Atlantic, and propose a transnational college of independent auditors as the institutional form in which they can be applied before legislators codify the Accord.

detail.abstract: We study single-stock leveraged ETFs, which obtain leverage through total-return swaps (TRSs). We focus on what we term Excess Financing Costs (EFCs), which differ from those implied by canonical models because (i) swap counterparties charge a spread over the floating benchmark rate, (ii) the funds hold little or no underlying stock, so swap interest rates apply to a larger financing base, and (iii) unrealized swap gains or losses imply variation through time in equity exposure relative to the financing base. For the full sample EFCs average 6.2% annualized, rising to 7.3% by the final quarter (several times larger than disclosed expense ratios) and are fully passed through to investors. We also show that fund managers partially mitigate these costs by selectively closing swaps with higher financing bases per dollar of equity exposure. ETFs with lower EFCs earn returns that are about 1.43% per year higher than high-EFC funds tracking the same stock.

detail.abstract: This paper examines what the price premium for cellular capability in high-end devices can reveal about the value of cellular standard-essential patents (SEPs) and the determination of FRAND royalties. We argue that the observed cellular premium is not a direct measure of SEP value. First, moving from the device-level premium to patent value requires identifying the appropriate technological counterfactual, accounting for implementation costs and complementary investments, and distinguishing currently enforceable patent rights from technology embodied in prior cellular standards or the public domain. Second, the premium itself is shaped by broader economic forces, including brand value, complementary innovation, market power, product-versioning strategies, and the option value consumers place on retaining the ability to activate cellular service in the future. We develop a simple real-options framework to illustrate the distinction between willingness to pay for cellular capability and willingness to pay for cellular service. Taken together, these considerations imply that cellular premiums may contain useful information about the economic importance of connectivity, but they are not self-sufficient benchmarks for SEP value or FRAND royalties. Royalty assessment instead requires evidence linking the observed premium to the incremental contribution of the relevant patented technology relative to feasible alternatives.

detail.abstract: I build a market index for sealed Magic: The Gathering booster boxes from 257 boxes and 136 monthly returns, July 2015 to October 2026, and take the capital asset pricing model to it. Before costs, an equal-weighted portfolio returned 18.7 log points a year (standard error 7.4), 13.6 outside 2021 and 8.8 since June 2021, with a long-run volatility of 24.8 per cent. The index explains 19 per cent of the monthly and 53 per cent of the annual variance of the median long-history box. The zero-beta model is rejected on sales prices by portfolios sorted on price and on age, and not on asking prices. Past winners earn less only on asking prices, expensive boxes only on sales prices. Out of sample no optimised rule beats equal weights after adjustment, and minimum variance lowers volatility by 5 per cent, not distinguishably from zero.
